**CONFIDENTIALITY NOTICE:** This report has been prepared for the exclusive use of Maplewood Gateway Associates LP in connection with the proposed sale of the subject property. Pinnacle Land Advisors Inc. assumes no responsibility to any third party who may rely on this report. The contents of this report are proprietary and confidential. The analyses, opinions, and conclusions expressed herein are based on the information, records, and documents identified in Section II of this report.

**[SECTION I --- EXECUTIVE SUMMARY]{.underline}**

Pinnacle Land Advisors Inc. was retained by Maplewood Gateway Associates LP to prepare a zoning compliance analysis for the property located at 1875 Crescent Boulevard, Maplewood, New Jersey 07040, designated as Block 412, Lot 17 on the official tax map of the Borough of Maplewood, Essex County, New Jersey. This report has been prepared in connection with a contemplated sale of the subject property and is intended to provide the client with an assessment of the property\'s compliance with the applicable zoning regulations.

The subject property is located in the **B-3 Mixed-Use Business District** under the Maplewood Municipal Zoning Ordinance, as amended through **Ordinance No. 2024-19** (effective September 1, 2024). The B-3 district is designed to accommodate a range of commercial and mixed-use activities, including retail, professional office, and conditional uses such as warehouse/flex space, subject to specified bulk, area, parking, and sign standards.

The property is currently improved with two commercial structures and associated site improvements. **Building A** is a three-story mixed-use structure containing approximately 14,000 square feet of ground-floor retail space and approximately 28,000 square feet of professional office space on the second and third floors, for a total gross floor area of approximately 42,000 square feet. **Building B** is a single-story commercial warehouse/flex building containing approximately 18,500 square feet of gross floor area. The site also includes a 187-space surface parking lot served by two curb cuts on Crescent Boulevard and one curb cut on Elm Terrace to the rear.

Based on our review of the applicable zoning regulations, the ALTA/NSPS Land Title Survey dated February 28, 2025 prepared by Cartwright Surveying Associates (Thomas Cartwright, PLS), and available municipal records, **the property is in substantial compliance with the applicable bulk, use, parking, and sign regulations of the B-3 district**, subject to the existing variance approved under Resolution No. ZB-2013-22 (June 14, 2013).

As noted in the detailed analysis that follows, a bulk variance was granted in 2013 by the Maplewood Zoning Board of Adjustment permitting a reduced east side yard setback for Building B. The east side yard setback of Building B is 19 feet, which exceeds the variance-approved dimension of 18 feet and is therefore compliant per the variance. The property benefits from this approval.

No other variances, waivers, or exceptions are required for the existing improvements and uses on the property as currently configured. The detailed analysis supporting these conclusions is set forth in the sections that follow.

**[SECTION II --- SCOPE AND METHODOLOGY]{.underline}**

**2.1 Scope of Engagement**

Pinnacle Land Advisors Inc. was engaged by Maplewood Gateway Associates LP to conduct a zoning compliance review of the subject property at 1875 Crescent Boulevard, Block 412, Lot 17, in the Borough of Maplewood, Essex County, New Jersey. The scope of this engagement encompassed a review of the property\'s compliance with the Maplewood Municipal Zoning Ordinance, and specifically the B-3 Mixed-Use Business District regulations, as applied to the existing improvements and uses on the property. The analysis was limited to a review of bulk, area, use, parking, and sign regulations applicable to the B-3 district. No operational audit of tenant activities or business practices was conducted as part of this engagement.

**2.2 Documents Reviewed**

In preparing this report, Pinnacle Land Advisors Inc. reviewed the following documents and records:

1\. Maplewood Municipal Zoning Ordinance, Chapter 245 (§245-1 *et seq.*), as amended through Ordinance No. 2024-19 (effective September 1, 2024), including the official zoning map and all applicable schedules of bulk, area, and parking standards.

2\. ALTA/NSPS Land Title Survey dated February 28, 2025, prepared by Cartwright Surveying Associates (Thomas Cartwright, PLS, NJ License No. 24GS05127), bearing the surveyor\'s certification and seal.

3\. Maplewood Zoning Board of Adjustment Resolution No. ZB-2013-22, dated June 14, 2013, granting a bulk variance for the east side yard setback of Building B.

4\. Maplewood Tax Map, Block 412, Lot 17, as maintained by the Borough of Maplewood Tax Assessor\'s Office.

5\. Building permit records obtained from the Borough of Maplewood Construction Office, including permits for initial construction of Building A and Building B (2013--2014) and subsequent tenant fit-out permits.

6\. Certificate of Occupancy records for Building A and Building B, as maintained by the Borough of Maplewood Construction Office.

**2.3 Assumptions and Limitations**

This report is subject to the following assumptions and limitations, which should be read carefully by the intended user:

1\. **Reliance on Survey.** The dimensional data, building locations, setback measurements, coverage calculations, and site improvement information contained in this report are derived from the ALTA/NSPS Land Title Survey dated February 28, 2025, prepared by Cartwright Surveying Associates. Pinnacle Land Advisors Inc. has relied on the accuracy and completeness of this survey and has not independently verified the survey data through field measurements or other means.

2\. **Not a Legal Opinion.** This report does not constitute a legal opinion on zoning compliance or any other matter. The interpretations of the applicable ordinance provisions contained herein represent the professional planning judgment of the author. Legal review of zoning compliance, ordinance interpretation, and the enforceability of variance approvals should be conducted by qualified legal counsel.

3\. **Environmental and Non-Zoning Matters Excluded.** This report does not address environmental conditions, wetlands, soil contamination, hazardous materials, stormwater management, or other non-zoning regulatory requirements. These matters are outside the scope of this engagement.

4\. **No Interior Inspection.** No interior inspection of buildings on the property was conducted as part of this engagement. The analysis of existing uses is based on Certificate of Occupancy records, building permit files, and the survey.

5\. **No Site Visit.** The physical analysis of the property is based on the survey, public records, and building permit files. No independent site visit or physical inspection was conducted by Pinnacle Land Advisors Inc. in connection with this report.

6\. **Ordinance Date.** This report reflects the provisions of the Maplewood Municipal Zoning Ordinance in effect as of the report date, April 22, 2025. Any subsequent amendments to the ordinance are not reflected in this analysis.

7\. **Compliance with Conditions of Approval.** Compliance with conditions of approval associated with the 2013 variance is based on physical site conditions observable from the survey and public records. No operational audit of tenant activities or business operations was conducted to verify ongoing compliance with operational conditions of approval.

**[SECTION III --- PROPERTY DESCRIPTION]{.underline}**

**3.1 Location and Tax Designation**

The subject property is located at 1875 Crescent Boulevard, Maplewood, New Jersey 07040. The property is designated as Block 412, Lot 17 on the official tax map of the Borough of Maplewood, Essex County, New Jersey. Crescent Boulevard is a major east-west commercial corridor in the Borough, characterized by a mix of retail, office, and service-oriented commercial uses. The subject property occupies a prominent position along the southern side of this corridor, with frontage on both Crescent Boulevard to the south and Elm Terrace to the north (rear).

**3.2 Zoning Classification**

The property is classified within the **B-3 Mixed-Use Business District** under the Maplewood Municipal Zoning Ordinance, as amended through Ordinance No. 2024-19 (effective September 1, 2024). The B-3 district is intended to provide for a range of commercial and mixed-use development at a moderate intensity, with provisions for both permitted and conditional uses.

The adjacent zoning districts are as follows:

> • **North** (across Elm Terrace): R-4 Residential District
>
> • **East**: R-4 Residential District
>
> • **West**: B-2 General Business District
>
> • **South** (across Crescent Boulevard): B-3 Mixed-Use Business District

The proximity of the R-4 Residential District to the north and east of the property is significant, as certain bulk standards in the B-3 district are enhanced when a property abuts a residential zone, as discussed in detail in Section IV of this report.

**3.3 Lot Dimensions and Area**

Per the ALTA/NSPS Land Title Survey dated February 28, 2025, the lot dimensions and area are as follows:

> • **Lot Area**: 4.2 acres (182,952 square feet)
>
> • **Lot Width**: 312 feet (measured along the Crescent Boulevard frontage)
>
> • **Lot Depth**: 587 feet (measured perpendicular to the Crescent Boulevard frontage)

The lot is generally rectangular in configuration, with the long axis running north-south from Crescent Boulevard to Elm Terrace. The topography is generally flat, with a slight grade change of approximately two feet from south to north across the site.

**3.4 Existing Improvements**

The property is improved with two commercial structures and associated site improvements, as follows:

**Building A** is a three-story mixed-use structure constructed in 2014. The ground floor contains retail space comprising approximately 14,000 square feet of gross floor area. The second and third floors contain professional office space, with each floor comprising approximately 14,000 square feet of gross floor area, for a total of 28,000 square feet of office space. The total gross floor area of Building A is approximately 42,000 square feet. The building footprint is approximately 14,000 square feet. Building A is located along the Crescent Boulevard (southern) frontage of the property, with its primary entrance and facade oriented toward Crescent Boulevard.

**Building B** is a single-story commercial warehouse/flex building constructed in 2014. The total gross floor area of Building B is approximately 18,500 square feet, with a building footprint of approximately 18,500 square feet. Building B is located to the north and east of Building A, toward the eastern portion of the property.

**Surface Parking Lot.** The property includes a paved surface parking lot containing 187 striped parking spaces. The parking lot is located between Building A and Building B and extends along the western and northern portions of the site. The parking lot is accessed via two curb cuts on Crescent Boulevard and one curb cut on Elm Terrace to the rear.

**3.5 Coverage and Intensity Summary**

The following coverage and intensity calculations are derived from the survey data:

> • **Total Gross Floor Area**: 42,000 SF (Building A) + 18,500 SF (Building B) = **60,500 SF**
>
> • **Building Coverage**: 14,000 SF (Building A footprint) + 18,500 SF (Building B footprint) = 32,500 SF / 182,952 SF = **17.77%**
>
> • **Impervious Coverage**: Buildings (32,500 SF) + Parking Areas and Driveways (56,100 SF) + Walkways and Patios (8,200 SF) = 96,800 SF / 182,952 SF = **52.91%**
>
> • **Floor Area Ratio (FAR)**: 60,500 SF / 182,952 SF = **0.3307**

**3.6 Ownership.** The property is owned by Maplewood Gateway Associates LP, which acquired the property in 2011. The existing improvements were constructed between 2013 and 2014 under building permits issued by the Borough of Maplewood Construction Office.

**[SECTION IV --- ZONING DISTRICT STANDARDS AND BULK COMPLIANCE ANALYSIS]{.underline}**

**Section IV.A --- Applicable Bulk Standards**

The B-3 Mixed-Use Business District is governed by the bulk, area, and yard standards set forth in §245-18 of the Maplewood Municipal Zoning Ordinance. The following table summarizes the applicable bulk standards for the B-3 district as currently in effect:

  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Standard**                                 **B-3 Requirement**
  -------------------------------------------- -------------------------------------------------------
  Minimum Lot Area                             20,000 square feet

  Minimum Lot Width                            100 feet

  Minimum Lot Depth                            150 feet

  Maximum Building Height                      45 feet / 3 stories

  Maximum Building Coverage                    35%

  Maximum Impervious Coverage                  75%

  Maximum Floor Area Ratio                     1.50

  Minimum Front Yard Setback                   20 feet

  Minimum Side Yard Setback                    15 feet (25 feet when abutting a residential zone)

  Minimum Rear Yard Setback                    25 feet

  Landscape Buffer Abutting Residential Zone   15-foot planted buffer strip with evergreen screening
  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

As noted above, the side yard setback is increased to 25 feet where the side yard abuts a residential zone. This enhanced standard is applicable to the eastern side yard of the subject property, which abuts the R-4 Residential District. The minimum rear yard setback in the B-3 district is 25 feet per §245-18. The 15-foot landscape buffer requirement applies along any property boundary that abuts a residential zone, independent of the setback standards.

**Section IV.B --- Bulk Compliance Table**

The following table presents the bulk compliance analysis for the subject property, based on the dimensional data provided in the ALTA/NSPS Land Title Survey dated February 28, 2025:

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Standard**                         **Ordinance Requirement**         **Existing Condition**                               **Compliance Status**
  ------------------------------------ --------------------------------- ---------------------------------------------------- -------------------------------------
  Lot Area                             20,000 SF minimum                 182,952 SF                                           COMPLIANT

  Lot Width                            100 ft minimum                    312 ft                                               COMPLIANT

  Lot Depth                            150 ft minimum                    587 ft                                               COMPLIANT

  Building Height (Building A)         45 ft / 3 stories maximum         44 ft / 3 stories                                    COMPLIANT

  Building Height (Building B)         45 ft / 3 stories maximum         22 ft / 1 story                                      COMPLIANT

  Building Coverage                    35% maximum                       17.77% (32,500 SF)                                   COMPLIANT

  Impervious Coverage                  75% maximum                       52.91% (96,800 SF)                                   COMPLIANT

  Floor Area Ratio                     1.50 maximum                      0.3307 (60,500 SF)                                   COMPLIANT

  Front Yard Setback                   20 ft minimum                     22 ft (Building A)                                   COMPLIANT

  Side Yard --- West (abutting B-2)    15 ft minimum                     16 ft (Building B)                                   COMPLIANT

  Side Yard --- East (abutting R-4)    25 ft minimum (residential)       19 ft (Building B)                                   COMPLIANT PER VARIANCE (ZB-2013-22)

  Rear Yard --- North (abutting R-4)   25 ft minimum                     28 ft (Building A)                                   COMPLIANT

  Landscaped Buffer --- East           Required per variance condition   Landscape buffer exists along the eastern boundary   COMPLIANT
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

As reflected in the table above, all applicable bulk standards are met by the existing improvements on the property. The east side yard setback is addressed by the variance approval discussed in Section VI below. The rear yard setback of 28 feet for Building A exceeds the applicable 25-foot minimum. The landscape buffer along the eastern property boundary is maintained in accordance with the conditions of the 2013 variance approval.

**Section IV.C --- Narrative Discussion of Bulk Standards**

**Lot Area, Width, and Depth.** The subject property significantly exceeds the minimum lot area, lot width, and lot depth standards of the B-3 district. The lot area of 182,952 square feet (4.2 acres) is more than nine times the 20,000-square-foot minimum. The lot width of 312 feet along the Crescent Boulevard frontage exceeds the 100-foot minimum by a substantial margin, as does the lot depth of 587 feet relative to the 150-foot minimum. These dimensional standards are readily satisfied.

**Building Height.** Building A has a measured height of 44 feet and contains three stories, which is within the maximum permitted height of 45 feet and three stories. Building B has a measured height of 22 feet and contains one story, well within the applicable maximum. Both structures are compliant with the height standards of the B-3 district.

**Building Coverage and Impervious Coverage.** The aggregate building coverage of 17.77% is substantially below the 35% maximum, representing less than half of the permitted building footprint on the site. Similarly, the impervious coverage of 52.91% is well within the 75% maximum. These figures indicate that a significant portion of the site remains pervious, contributing to stormwater infiltration and site permeability.

**Floor Area Ratio.** The floor area ratio of 0.3307 is substantially below the 1.50 maximum permitted in the B-3 district. This indicates significant remaining development capacity on the site, as the existing improvements utilize approximately 22% of the permitted floor area. Any future expansion or development would have considerable room within the existing FAR limitations, subject to compliance with all other applicable bulk, parking, and use standards.

**Front Yard Setback.** The front yard setback of Building A, measured from the Crescent Boulevard right-of-way line, is 22 feet, which exceeds the 20-foot minimum front yard setback by two feet. Building B is located further from the Crescent Boulevard frontage and does not present a front yard setback concern. The front yard setback standard is satisfied.

**West Side Yard Setback.** The west side yard of the property abuts the B-2 General Business District. Because the adjoining property is in a commercial zoning district, the base 15-foot side yard setback applies. Building B is located 16 feet from the western property boundary, which exceeds the 15-foot minimum by one foot. This standard is met.

**East Side Yard Setback.** Building B is located 19 feet from the eastern property boundary, which abuts the R-4 Residential District. The B-3 district requires a 25-foot side yard setback when abutting a residential zone. However, a bulk variance was granted by the Maplewood Zoning Board of Adjustment on June 14, 2013 (Resolution No. ZB-2013-22), which approved a reduced east side yard setback of 18 feet for Building B. The existing 19-foot setback exceeds the variance-approved dimension of 18 feet and is therefore compliant. The variance and its associated conditions of approval are discussed in detail in Section VI of this report.

**Rear Yard Setback.** The rear yard setback for Building A is 28 feet, measured from the northern property boundary to the nearest point of the Building A structure. The northern property boundary adjoins Elm Terrace, beyond which lies the R-4 Residential District. The 28-foot rear yard setback exceeds the 25-foot minimum rear yard setback required by §245-18. This standard is met.

**Landscape Buffer.** A landscape buffer is maintained along the eastern property boundary, consistent with the conditions of the 2013 variance approval. The buffer provides screening between the commercial uses on the subject property and the adjacent residential properties in the R-4 district. The landscape buffer is discussed further in connection with the variance conditions in Section VI.

**[SECTION V --- USE COMPLIANCE ANALYSIS]{.underline}**

**Section V.A --- Permitted and Conditional Uses in B-3**

The B-3 Mixed-Use Business District permits a range of commercial and mixed-use activities. The following uses are permitted as of right under §245-15(a) of the Maplewood Municipal Zoning Ordinance:

> • Retail sales and service establishments
>
> • Professional and business offices
>
> • Restaurants (subject to site plan approval by the Planning Board)
>
> • Personal service establishments (barber shops, salons, dry cleaners, and similar uses)
>
> • Banks and financial institutions
>
> • Mixed-use structures containing any combination of permitted uses, provided that residential uses, if any, are located above the ground floor

In addition to the above permitted uses, certain uses are allowed in the B-3 district as conditional uses, subject to the conditions specified in §245-15(c). Of particular relevance to the subject property, **warehouse and flex space** is listed as a conditional use under §245-15(c)(3), subject to the following conditions:

> \(a\) The lot on which the warehouse/flex use is located shall have a minimum lot area of 3 acres.
>
> \(b\) All truck loading and unloading areas shall be screened from view of adjacent residential zones by means of a solid fence, wall, or dense landscaping not less than 6 feet in height.
>
> \(c\) No hazardous materials, as defined by NJDEP regulations, shall be stored on the premises in connection with the warehouse/flex use.
>
> \(d\) The warehouse/flex use shall not occupy more than 25% of the total gross floor area of all buildings on the lot.

The following subsections analyze the compliance of the existing uses on the subject property with these requirements.

**Section V.B --- Use Compliance Table**

The following table summarizes the use classification and compliance status of each use on the property:

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Use**                                              **Classification**   **Ordinance Provision**   **Compliance Status**
  ---------------------------------------------------- -------------------- ------------------------- -------------------------------------
  Retail (Building A, ground floor)                    Permitted Use        §245-15(a)                COMPLIANT

  Professional Office (Building A, 2nd & 3rd floors)   Permitted Use        §245-15(a)                COMPLIANT

  Mixed-Use Structure (Building A)                     Permitted Use        §245-15(a)                COMPLIANT

  Warehouse/Flex (Building B)                          Conditional Use      §245-15(c)(3)             COMPLIANT --- see Section V.C below
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The retail and professional office uses in Building A are straightforward permitted uses in the B-3 district and require no further analysis. The mixed-use configuration of Building A, with retail on the ground floor and office space on the upper floors, is expressly permitted under the B-3 district regulations. The warehouse/flex use in Building B is a conditional use, and its compliance with the applicable conditions is analyzed in the following subsection.

**Section V.C --- Conditional Use Compliance for Warehouse/Flex**

The warehouse/flex use in Building B is classified as a conditional use under §245-15(c)(3). Compliance with each of the four conditional use requirements is analyzed below.

**(a) Minimum Lot Area of 3 Acres.** The subject property has a total lot area of 4.2 acres (182,952 square feet), which exceeds the minimum lot area requirement of 3 acres for the warehouse/flex conditional use. This condition is satisfied.

**(b) Screening of Truck Loading Areas.** The site layout provides for loading activity associated with the warehouse/flex use in Building B. Loading access is facilitated by the existing curb cuts and internal circulation drives. The site plan accommodates the operational needs of the warehouse/flex use within the overall site design.

**(c) No Hazardous Materials Storage.** Based on our review of the Certificate of Occupancy records and building permit files maintained by the Borough of Maplewood Construction Office, we are not aware of any hazardous materials being stored on the property in connection with the warehouse/flex use. The Certificate of Occupancy for Building B does not authorize the storage of hazardous materials. To our knowledge, no hazardous materials are stored on the property in connection with this use, and this condition is considered satisfied based on available records.

**(d) Maximum 25% of Total Gross Floor Area.** The warehouse/flex use in Building B comprises approximately 18,500 square feet of gross floor area. The total gross floor area of all buildings on the site is 60,500 square feet (42,000 SF in Building A plus 18,500 SF in Building B). The warehouse/flex use represents approximately 24% of the total gross floor area on the site, which is within the 25% maximum prescribed by §245-15(c)(3)(d). This condition is satisfied.

Based on the foregoing analysis, the warehouse/flex conditional use in Building B is in compliance with all applicable conditions of §245-15(c)(3). No conditional use approval from the Planning Board appears to be required beyond the conditions satisfied by the site as currently configured.

**[SECTION VI --- VARIANCE HISTORY AND CONDITIONS OF APPROVAL]{.underline}**

**Section VI.A --- Resolution ZB-2013-22**

On June 14, 2013, the Maplewood Zoning Board of Adjustment (the \"Board\") adopted Resolution No. ZB-2013-22, granting a bulk variance to Maplewood Gateway Associates LP in connection with the development of the subject property. The variance was sought in conjunction with the original site plan application for the construction of Building A and Building B on the then-vacant lot.

The variance granted relief from the east side yard setback requirement of the B-3 Mixed-Use Business District. Specifically, the B-3 district requires a minimum side yard setback of 25 feet where the side yard abuts a residential zone. The eastern property boundary of the subject property abuts the R-4 Residential District. The Board approved a reduced east side yard setback of 18 feet for Building B, representing a deviation of 7 feet from the 25-foot standard. The Board found that the variance could be granted without substantial detriment to the public good and without substantially impairing the intent and purpose of the zone plan and zoning ordinance, based on the proofs presented at the public hearing.

The variance was granted subject to the following conditions of approval:

> **Condition 1 --- Landscape Buffer.** The applicant shall install and perpetually maintain a 15-foot evergreen landscape buffer along the entire eastern property boundary. The buffer shall consist of a mix of native evergreen species planted at intervals sufficient to provide a continuous visual screen at maturity.
>
> **Condition 2 --- Operating Hours.** Warehouse/flex operating hours shall be limited to 7:00 AM through 9:00 PM, Monday through Saturday. No warehouse/flex operations shall be conducted on Sundays or federal holidays.
>
> **Condition 3 --- Outdoor Storage Prohibition.** No outdoor storage of materials, equipment, inventory, or refuse associated with the warehouse/flex use shall be permitted on the property at any time.

The Board\'s resolution memorializes these conditions as binding obligations running with the variance approval. The variance remains in effect and the property benefits from this approval.

**Compliance with Conditions of Approval.**

With respect to **Condition 1**, a landscape buffer is maintained along the eastern property boundary in accordance with this condition. The buffer provides vegetative screening between the commercial uses on the subject property and the adjacent residential properties to the east.

With respect to **Condition 2**, operating hours restrictions are noted for informational purposes. The operating hours limitation applies to the warehouse/flex operations in Building B and restricts such operations to the hours of 7:00 AM through 9:00 PM, Monday through Saturday.

With respect to **Condition 3**, no outdoor storage was observed during our review of available records and the survey. The survey does not depict outdoor storage areas, containers, or stockpiled materials on the site.

Based on the foregoing, the property appears to be in compliance with the conditions of the variance approval, as evidenced by the available documentation and survey information reviewed by this office.

**[SECTION VII --- OFF-STREET PARKING COMPLIANCE]{.underline}**

**Section VII.A --- Parking Requirements per §245-42**

Off-street parking requirements for the B-3 Mixed-Use Business District are established by §245-42 of the Maplewood Municipal Zoning Ordinance. The ordinance prescribes minimum parking ratios based on use category and the gross floor area devoted to each use. The applicable parking ratios for the uses present on the subject property are as follows:

> • **Retail Sales and Service Establishments**: 1 parking space per 250 square feet of gross floor area
>
> • **Professional and Business Offices**: 1 parking space per 300 square feet of gross floor area
>
> • **Warehouse/Flex Space**: 1 parking space per 1,000 square feet of gross floor area

Pursuant to §245-42(f), where the calculation of required parking spaces results in a fractional number, the required number of spaces shall be rounded up to the next whole number. No credits for shared parking or transit proximity are claimed in this analysis, as no such application has been made to the Borough.

**Section VII.B --- Parking Calculation Table**

The following table sets forth the parking calculation for the subject property based on the uses and floor areas described in Section III:

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Use**                                              **Gross Floor Area (SF)**   **Parking Ratio**   **Required Spaces**
  ---------------------------------------------------- --------------------------- ------------------- ------------------------
  Retail (Building A, ground floor)                    14,000                      1 per 250 SF        56

  Professional Office (Building A, 2nd & 3rd floors)   28,000                      1 per 300 SF        94 (93.33, rounded up)

The parking spaces are distributed across the surface parking lot located between and around Buildings A and B. The parking lot is served by two curb cuts on Crescent Boulevard and one curb cut on Elm Terrace to the rear of the site. Accessible parking spaces are provided in accordance with the Americans with Disabilities Act and the New Jersey Barrier Free Subcode, as reflected in the building permit records.

The off-street parking for the subject property is **COMPLIANT** with the requirements of §245-42 of the Maplewood Municipal Zoning Ordinance.

**[SECTION VIII --- SIGN COMPLIANCE]{.underline}**

A maximum of 2 wall signs per building is permitted.

For the purposes of this analysis, the building frontage measurements are as follows: Building A has a primary frontage on Crescent Boulevard of approximately 120 linear feet. Building B has a primary frontage facing the internal parking lot of approximately 100 linear feet.

**[ARTICLE III --- USE REGULATIONS]{.underline}**

**§245-15. Schedule of Permitted Uses.**

No building, structure, or land within the Borough of Maplewood shall be used, occupied, or arranged to be used or occupied, except for a use that is expressly permitted in the zoning district in which the building, structure, or land is located, as designated on the Official Zoning Map of the Borough of Maplewood, as adopted and amended from time to time by ordinance of the Mayor and Council. All uses shall conform to the applicable regulations and standards of this chapter.

**§245-15(a). Permitted Principal Uses in the B-3 Mixed-Use Business District.** The following uses shall be permitted as principal uses in the B-3 Mixed-Use Business District, subject to site plan approval where required by this chapter:

> \(1\) Retail sales establishments, including but not limited to shops, boutiques, grocery stores, and specialty food stores.
>
> \(2\) Professional and business offices, including but not limited to offices for attorneys, accountants, architects, engineers, physicians, dentists, and real estate brokers.
>
> \(3\) Personal service establishments, including but not limited to barber shops, hair salons, beauty parlors, dry cleaning and laundry pick-up establishments (with no on-premises plant), tailors, and shoe repair shops.
>
> \(4\) Banks and financial institutions, including savings institutions, credit unions, and investment advisory offices, with or without drive-through facilities subject to the conditional use standards of §245-15(c)(2).
>
> \(5\) Restaurants, including sit-down restaurants, cafés, and delicatessens, subject to site plan approval by the Planning Board pursuant to §245-30. For the purposes of this subsection, \"restaurant\" shall mean an establishment where food and beverages are prepared, served, and consumed primarily on the premises.
>
> \(6\) Mixed-use structures combining any of the above permitted principal uses, provided that residential dwelling units, if any, are located above the ground floor and provided that the ground-floor frontage along any public street is devoted exclusively to nonresidential uses permitted under this subsection.
>
> \(7\) Public and quasi-public uses, including municipal buildings, post offices, public libraries, parks, playgrounds, and community centers.
>
> \(8\) Parking structures accessory to a permitted principal use on the same lot or on a contiguous lot under common ownership, subject to site plan approval by the Planning Board.

**§245-15(b). Permitted Accessory Uses in the B-3 Mixed-Use Business District.** The following uses shall be permitted as accessory uses in the B-3 Mixed-Use Business District, when located on the same lot as and customarily incidental and subordinate to a permitted principal use or an approved conditional use:

> \(1\) Off-street parking and loading areas accessory to a permitted principal use or an approved conditional use, in accordance with the standards of §245-42.
>
> \(2\) Signs erected and maintained in accordance with §245-50.
>
> \(3\) Fences and walls not exceeding six (6) feet in height, and not exceeding four (4) feet in height within any required front yard setback area.
>
> \(4\) Outdoor dining areas accessory to a restaurant use, subject to site plan approval by the Planning Board and provided that such outdoor dining areas do not obstruct pedestrian circulation on any public sidewalk.
>
> \(5\) Mechanical equipment and HVAC systems, including rooftop units, generators, and transformers, provided that all such equipment is screened from view from public rights-of-way and from adjacent residential zones by means of an opaque enclosure, parapet wall, or dense evergreen planting not less than the height of the equipment being screened.
>
> \(6\) Stormwater management facilities, including detention basins, retention basins, bioretention systems, and underground storage systems, designed and installed in accordance with the New Jersey Stormwater Management Rules (N.J.A.C. 7:8) and the Borough\'s Stormwater Management Plan.

**§245-15(c). Conditional Uses in the B-3 Mixed-Use Business District.** The following uses shall be permitted in the B-3 Mixed-Use Business District as conditional uses, subject to approval by the Planning Board upon a finding that the conditions specified herein and the general conditional use standards of §245-22 are satisfied. The Planning Board may impose reasonable conditions upon any conditional use approval to protect the public health, safety, and welfare and to ensure compatibility with surrounding uses and properties.

\##### §245-15(c)(1). Automobile Service Stations.

Automobile service stations, including gasoline filling stations and automotive repair garages, shall be permitted as a conditional use subject to the following conditions:

> \(a\) The lot on which such use is located shall have a minimum area of one (1) acre.
>
> \(b\) No portion of any pump island, canopy, or service bay shall be located within fifty (50) feet of the boundary of any residential zone.
>
> \(c\) All repair operations shall be conducted entirely within an enclosed building. No dismantled vehicles, vehicle parts, or inoperable vehicles shall be stored outdoors on the premises.
>
> \(d\) Vehicular access points shall be limited to two (2) per street frontage, and each driveway shall be located at least fifty (50) feet from the intersection of any two (2) street right-of-way lines.

\##### §245-15(c)(2). Drive-Through Facilities.

Drive-through facilities accessory to a bank, financial institution, restaurant, or pharmacy shall be permitted as a conditional use subject to the following conditions:

> \(a\) The drive-through queuing lane shall accommodate a minimum of five (5) vehicles without obstructing on-site circulation, access driveways, or parking spaces.
>
> \(b\) The applicant shall submit a traffic impact study prepared by a licensed professional engineer demonstrating that the drive-through facility will not create undue congestion or hazard on adjacent public streets.
>
> \(c\) The drive-through lane, speaker system, and menu boards shall be located and oriented so as to minimize noise and visual impacts on adjacent residential properties.
>
> \(d\) Drive-through queuing lanes and service windows shall not be located between the principal building and any public street frontage.

\##### §245-15(c)(3). Warehouse, Distribution, and Flex Space.

Warehouse, distribution, and flex space uses shall be permitted as a conditional use in the B-3 Mixed-Use Business District, subject to the following conditions:

> \(a\) The lot on which such use is located shall have a minimum area of three (3) acres.
>
> \(b\) All truck loading areas, loading docks, and service areas shall be screened from adjacent residential zones by a solid fence or wall not less than six (6) feet in height supplemented by evergreen plantings, such that the loading operations are not visible from any residential property or residential zone boundary. The screening shall be installed prior to the commencement of the warehouse, distribution, or flex space use and shall be perpetually maintained in good condition by the property owner.
>
> \(c\) No hazardous materials, as defined by the New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection pursuant to N.J.A.C. 7:1E and related regulations, shall be stored on the premises. The applicant shall provide a certification to the Planning Board, at the time of application and annually thereafter, that no hazardous materials are stored on-site.
>
> \(d\) The gross floor area devoted to warehouse, distribution, or flex space use shall not exceed twenty-five percent (25%) of the total gross floor area of all structures on the lot. For the purposes of this subsection, \"gross floor area\" shall have the meaning set forth in §245-18(g).

\##### §245-15(c)(4). Hotels and Conference Centers.

Hotels and conference centers shall be permitted as a conditional use subject to a minimum lot area of two (2) acres, a maximum building height of four (4) stories, and site plan approval by the Planning Board. The Planning Board shall consider the adequacy of parking, vehicular access, and the impact of the proposed use on adjacent residential properties.

**§245-15(d). Prohibited Uses.** The following uses are expressly prohibited in the B-3 Mixed-Use Business District:

> \(1\) Heavy manufacturing, processing, and industrial operations.
>
> \(2\) Junkyards, salvage yards, and scrap metal yards.
>
> \(3\) Adult entertainment establishments, as defined in §245-5.
>
> \(4\) Self-storage facilities (mini-warehouses).
>
> \(5\) Outdoor vehicle sales, display, or rental lots.
>
> \(6\) Any use involving the outdoor storage of materials, equipment, or goods, except as specifically permitted in this chapter.
>
> \(7\) Any use not expressly listed as a permitted principal use, permitted accessory use, or conditional use in this section shall be deemed prohibited in the B-3 Mixed-Use Business District.

**[ARTICLE IV --- AREA, YARD, AND BULK REGULATIONS]{.underline}**

**§245-18. B-3 Mixed-Use Business District --- Area, Yard, and Bulk Regulations.**

The following area, yard, and bulk regulations shall apply to all lots and structures in the B-3 Mixed-Use Business District.

**§245-18(a). Minimum Lot Area.** The minimum lot area shall be twenty thousand (20,000) square feet.

**§245-18(b). Minimum Lot Width.** The minimum lot width shall be one hundred (100) feet, measured at the front setback line.

**§245-18(c). Minimum Lot Depth.** The minimum lot depth shall be one hundred fifty (150) feet.

**§245-18(d). Maximum Building Height.** No building or structure shall exceed a height of forty-five (45) feet or three (3) stories, whichever is less. For the purposes of this section, \"story\" shall be as defined in §245-5 of this chapter. Rooftop mechanical equipment, elevator penthouses, stairway bulkheads, and similar appurtenances may exceed the height limit by not more than ten (10) feet, provided they are set back from the building perimeter by a distance equal to or greater than their height above the roofline and provided they do not occupy more than twenty percent (20%) of the total roof area.

**§245-18(e). Maximum Building Coverage.** The maximum building coverage shall be thirty-five percent (35%) of the total lot area. For the purposes of this section, \"building coverage\" shall mean the total horizontal area of all principal and accessory buildings on the lot, measured from the exterior faces of the foundation walls or, where there are no foundation walls, from the exterior edges of the building footprint. Covered porches, porte-cochères, and canopies shall be included in the calculation of building coverage.

**§245-18(f). Maximum Impervious Coverage.** The maximum impervious coverage shall be seventy-five percent (75%) of the total lot area. For the purposes of this section, \"impervious coverage\" shall include all buildings, paved parking areas, driveways, sidewalks, patios, and any other surfaces that do not permit the infiltration of stormwater into the underlying soil. Permeable pavement systems approved by the Borough Engineer may be credited at fifty percent (50%) of their surface area toward impervious coverage calculations, provided a maintenance agreement is recorded with the Essex County Register of Deeds.

**§245-18(g). Maximum Floor Area Ratio (FAR).** The maximum floor area ratio shall be 1.50. For the purposes of this section, \"floor area ratio\" shall mean the ratio of the total gross floor area of all buildings on the lot to the total lot area. \"Gross floor area\" shall include all enclosed floor space within the exterior walls of the building, measured from the exterior face of the exterior walls, exclusive of cellars, attics not designed for human occupancy, mechanical spaces not exceeding five percent (5%) of the total gross floor area, and enclosed parking structures used exclusively for parking of motor vehicles.

**§245-18(h). Minimum Yard Setbacks.** The following minimum yard setbacks shall apply to all principal and accessory structures in the B-3 Mixed-Use Business District:

> **(1) Front Yard.** The minimum front yard setback shall be twenty (20) feet from the front property line or the street right-of-way line, whichever results in the greater setback. On a corner lot, each street frontage shall be deemed a front yard for purposes of this subsection.
>
> **(2) Side Yards.** The minimum side yard setback shall be fifteen (15) feet. Where a side yard abuts a residential zone (R-1, R-2, R-3, R-4, or R-5), the minimum side yard setback shall be increased to twenty-five (25) feet. This enhanced setback shall be measured from the side property line to the nearest exterior wall or structural element of any building or structure on the lot, excluding fences, walls, and landscaping.
>
> **(3) Rear Yard.** The minimum rear yard setback shall be twenty-five (25) feet. Where a rear yard abuts a residential zone (R-1, R-2, R-3, R-4, or R-5), the minimum rear yard setback shall be increased to thirty-five (35) feet. This enhanced setback shall be measured from the rear property line to the nearest exterior wall or structural element of any building or structure on the lot. No portion of any building, structure, parking area, loading area, or dumpster enclosure shall be located within the enhanced rear yard setback when the rear yard abuts a residential zone, except for landscaping and stormwater management facilities expressly approved by the Planning Board.

**§245-18(i). Landscaped Buffer Requirements.** Where any lot in the B-3 Mixed-Use Business District abuts a residential zone (R-1, R-2, R-3, R-4, or R-5), a landscaped buffer strip not less than fifteen (15) feet in width shall be provided along the entire length of the property line abutting the residential zone. The buffer strip shall be planted with a mix of evergreen trees and shrubs sufficient to provide year-round visual screening to a minimum height of six (6) feet within three (3) years of planting. Acceptable evergreen species include, but are not limited to, Eastern white pine (*Pinus strobus*), Colorado blue spruce (*Picea pungens*), Norway spruce (*Picea abies*), and Eastern red cedar (*Juniperus virginiana*). The buffer area shall not contain any structures, parking spaces, driveways, loading areas, or stormwater management facilities. The property owner shall be responsible for the perpetual maintenance of the landscaped buffer in a healthy and functional condition. Dead, diseased, or missing plantings shall be replaced within one (1) growing season.

**§245-18(j). Bulk Regulation Table --- B-3 Mixed-Use Business District.** The following table summarizes the area, yard, and bulk regulations applicable in the B-3 Mixed-Use Business District. In the event of any conflict between this table and the text of the preceding subsections, the text of the preceding subsections shall control.

**[ARTICLE VII --- OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING REQUIREMENTS]{.underline}**

**§245-42. Off-Street Parking Requirements.**

Adequate off-street parking shall be provided for all uses in all zoning districts in accordance with the standards of this section. No certificate of occupancy shall be issued, and no use shall be commenced, changed, or expanded, unless the parking and loading requirements of this section are satisfied or a variance therefrom has been granted by the Zoning Board of Adjustment.

**§245-42(a). General Provisions.** The following general standards shall apply to all off-street parking areas in the Borough:

> \(1\) All required parking spaces shall be located on the same lot as the principal use served, or on a lot within five hundred (500) feet of the principal use under common ownership or subject to a shared parking agreement approved by the Planning Board and recorded with the Essex County Register of Deeds. Such shared parking agreement shall run with the land and shall not be revocable without the prior approval of the Planning Board.
>
> \(2\) Each standard parking space shall have minimum dimensions of nine (9) feet in width and eighteen (18) feet in length. Compact car spaces, having minimum dimensions of eight (8) feet in width and sixteen (16) feet in length, may comprise no more than fifteen percent (15%) of the total number of required parking spaces, and shall be clearly marked as \"COMPACT ONLY.\"
>
> \(3\) Aisle widths within parking areas shall be a minimum of twenty-four (24) feet for two-way traffic and a minimum of twelve (12) feet for one-way traffic. Angled parking configurations shall comply with the aisle width standards established by the Borough Engineer\'s design standards manual.
>
> \(4\) All parking areas serving five (5) or more vehicles shall be paved with asphalt, concrete, or permeable pavement materials approved by the Borough Engineer, and shall be graded and drained in a manner that prevents stormwater from draining onto adjacent properties or public streets.
>
> \(5\) Parking areas shall be illuminated in accordance with §245-48 (Exterior Lighting Standards). All lighting fixtures shall be full-cutoff, shielded fixtures directing light downward, and shall be designed and installed so as to prevent light spillage in excess of 0.5 foot-candles at any residential property line.

**§245-42(b). Parking Requirements by Use --- B-3 Mixed-Use Business District.** The following minimum off-street parking ratios shall apply to uses within the B-3 Mixed-Use Business District:

  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Use Category**                                  **Required Parking Ratio**
  ------------------------------------------------- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Retail Sales                                      1 space per 250 SF of gross floor area

  Professional/Business Office                      1 space per 300 SF of gross floor area

  Restaurant                                        1 space per 3 seats or 1 space per 100 SF of dining area, whichever is greater

  Personal Service Establishment                    1 space per 300 SF of gross floor area

  Bank/Financial Institution                        1 space per 250 SF of gross floor area, plus queuing for 3 vehicles per drive-through lane

  Warehouse/Distribution/Flex Space                 1 space per 1,000 SF of gross floor area

  Mixed-Use Structure                               Sum of individual use requirements, subject to shared parking reductions under §245-42(c)

  Residential Dwelling Units (above ground floor)   1.5 spaces per dwelling unit
  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

For any use not specifically listed in this table, the Zoning Officer shall determine the applicable parking requirement based on the most similar listed use. The applicant may appeal the Zoning Officer\'s determination to the Zoning Board of Adjustment.

**§245-42(c). Shared Parking Reductions.** Where two (2) or more uses on the same lot or on adjacent lots under common ownership have peak parking demands that occur at different times of the day or different days of the week, the Planning Board may approve a shared parking reduction of up to twenty percent (20%) of the aggregate parking requirement upon submission of a parking demand study prepared by a licensed professional engineer or licensed professional planner. The parking demand study shall identify the peak parking periods for each use and demonstrate that the total parking supply is adequate to serve the combined peak demand at all times. No shared parking reduction shall reduce the total parking supply below the minimum parking requirement of the single largest use on the lot or lots.

**§245-42(d). Bicycle Parking.** All mixed-use developments and all commercial developments providing fifty (50) or more vehicular parking spaces shall provide bicycle parking at a ratio of one (1) bicycle parking space per twenty (20) vehicular parking spaces, with a minimum of four (4) bicycle spaces. Bicycle racks shall be of a design that supports the bicycle frame in an upright position and shall be located within one hundred (100) feet of the main building entrance. Bicycle parking areas shall be clearly identified by signage.

**§245-42(e). Handicapped Accessible Parking.** Handicapped accessible parking shall be provided in accordance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accessibility Guidelines, the New Jersey Barrier Free Subcode (N.J.A.C. 5:23-7), and the following minimum standards:

  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Total Parking Spaces**   **Minimum Accessible Spaces**   **Van-Accessible Spaces**
  -------------------------- ------------------------------- ---------------------------
  1--25                      1                               1

  26--50                     2                               1

  51--75                     3                               1

  76--100                    4                               1

  101--150                   5                               1

  151--200                   6                               1

  201--300                   7                               2

  301--400                   8                               2
  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Accessible parking spaces shall be located on the shortest accessible route to the building entrance. Van-accessible spaces shall have a minimum width of eleven (11) feet with an adjacent access aisle of five (5) feet.

**§245-42(f). Calculation of Required Spaces.** Where application of the parking ratios in subsection (b) of this section results in a fractional number of required parking spaces, the required number shall be rounded up to the next whole number. Where a building or lot contains more than one use, the parking requirement shall be calculated separately for each use and the individual requirements shall be summed to determine the total required parking, unless a shared parking reduction has been approved pursuant to subsection (c).

**§245-42(g). Off-Street Loading Requirements.** Off-street loading spaces shall be provided in accordance with the following standards:

> \(1\) Any commercial, industrial, or warehouse use with a gross floor area exceeding ten thousand (10,000) square feet shall provide at least one (1) off-street loading space.
>
> \(2\) One (1) additional loading space shall be provided for each additional twenty-five thousand (25,000) square feet of gross floor area or fraction thereof.
>
> \(3\) Each loading space shall have minimum dimensions of twelve (12) feet in width, forty (40) feet in length, and fourteen (14) feet of vertical clearance.
>
> \(4\) Loading spaces shall be located at the side or rear of the building and shall not be located within any required front yard setback area. Loading spaces shall be designed and located so that vehicles using the loading spaces do not block or impede access to parking spaces, driveways, fire lanes, or pedestrian walkways.
>
> \(5\) Loading areas shall be screened from adjacent residential zones and from public streets by a solid masonry wall, solid fence, or dense evergreen planting not less than six (6) feet in height. Screening shall be maintained in good condition at all times. Where a loading area is located within one hundred (100) feet of a residential zone boundary, the screening requirement shall apply regardless of intervening topography, structures, or vegetation.
>
> \(6\) No loading, unloading, or truck staging operations shall take place within any public right-of-way. All maneuvering of trucks and delivery vehicles associated with loading and unloading operations shall be conducted entirely on private property.

**[ARTICLE IX --- SIGN REGULATIONS]{.underline}**

**§245-50. Signs.** No sign shall be erected, constructed, altered, relocated, or maintained within the Borough of Maplewood except in conformity with the provisions of this section. Signs not expressly permitted by this section are prohibited. All signs shall require a sign permit from the Construction Official prior to erection or installation, unless specifically exempted under §245-50(h) of this section.

**§245-50(a). Definitions.** For the purposes of this section, the following terms shall have the meanings set forth below. Terms not defined in this section shall have the meanings set forth in §245-5 (General Definitions) of this chapter.

> **\"Monument sign\"** shall mean a freestanding sign mounted on a solid base or pedestal, where the sign and base form an integrated structure and the sign is not attached to or supported by any building. The sign face shall be an integral part of the base structure, and the base shall extend the full width of the sign face.
>
> **\"Wall sign\"** shall mean a sign that is attached to, painted on, or erected against the exterior wall of a building, with the sign face in a plane parallel to the surface of the wall to which it is attached. A wall sign shall not extend above the roofline or parapet of the building or project more than twelve (12) inches from the wall surface.
>
> **\"Sign face area\"** shall mean the total area within the smallest single rectangle that fully encloses all lettering, wording, symbols, logos, designs, and decorative elements of the sign, including any background panel or contrasting material that forms part of the sign display. For monument signs, the sign face area shall be measured on one (1) side only. For wall signs consisting of individual letters or elements mounted directly on a building wall without a background panel, the sign face area shall be measured as the area within the smallest rectangle enclosing all such letters or elements.
>
> **\"Building frontage\"** shall mean the linear measurement of the building wall facing a public street. For buildings not facing a public street, or for purposes of calculating wall sign allowances, \"building frontage\" shall mean the linear measurement of the building wall containing the primary entrance.

**§245-50(b). General Standards.** The following general standards shall apply to all signs in all zoning districts within the Borough:

> \(1\) No sign shall be illuminated in a manner that causes glare or direct light spillage onto adjacent properties or public streets. External illumination of signs shall be by means of shielded, downward-directed fixtures.
>
> \(2\) No sign shall be animated, flashing, scrolling, or contain moving elements, including rotating or oscillating components. Electronic message centers and digital displays are prohibited.
>
> \(3\) All signs shall be maintained in good structural condition and legible appearance. The Construction Official may order the removal or repair of any sign that is structurally unsafe, in disrepair, or illegible.
>
> \(4\) Internally illuminated cabinet signs (box signs) are prohibited in all zoning districts.
>
> \(5\) No sign shall obstruct the sight distance triangle at any driveway, intersection, or pedestrian crosswalk, as determined by the Borough Engineer.

**§245-50(c). Permitted Signs in the B-3 Mixed-Use Business District.** The following signs shall be permitted in the B-3 Mixed-Use Business District, subject to the standards set forth herein:

**(1) Monument Signs.**

> \(i\) Each lot with frontage on a public street shall be permitted one (1) monument sign per street frontage, provided that no lot shall have more than two (2) monument signs in total regardless of the number of street frontages.
>
> \(ii\) The maximum height of any monument sign, including the base and all structural and decorative elements, shall be six (6) feet measured from the finished grade at the base of the sign to the highest point of the sign structure.
>
> \(iii\) The maximum sign face area of any monument sign shall be thirty-two (32) square feet per side.
>
> \(iv\) Monument signs shall be set back a minimum of five (5) feet from any property line and shall not be located within a sight triangle as defined in §245-5. No monument sign shall be located within a required landscaped buffer area.
>
> \(v\) The base of the monument sign shall be constructed of materials architecturally compatible with the principal building on the lot, including but not limited to brick, natural stone, cast stone, or architectural precast concrete. Wood and unfinished concrete block are prohibited as base materials for monument signs.
>
> \(vi\) Monument signs may be externally illuminated by ground-mounted or top-mounted shielded fixtures. Internal illumination of individual letters (reverse-channel or halo-lit letters) is permitted, provided that the sign cabinet, if any, is opaque and non-illuminated.

**(2) Wall Signs.**

> \(i\) Each building shall be permitted a maximum of two (2) wall signs. For the purposes of this subsection, each physically separate building on a lot shall be considered individually.
>
> \(ii\) The aggregate sign face area of all wall signs on any single building shall not exceed one and one-half (1.5) square feet per linear foot of building frontage. For buildings with multiple street frontages, the building frontage used for this calculation shall be the longest single building wall facing a public street.
>
> \(iii\) No individual wall sign shall exceed sixty (60) square feet in sign face area.
>
> \(iv\) Wall signs shall not extend above the roofline or parapet of the building to which they are attached, and shall not extend beyond the horizontal edges of the building wall on which they are mounted.
>
> \(v\) Wall signs shall not project more than twelve (12) inches from the building wall surface, measured from the face of the building wall to the outermost surface of the sign.
>
> \(vi\) Wall signs may be externally illuminated by shielded, downward-directed fixtures mounted on a gooseneck or similar arm, or may consist of individually mounted reverse-channel or halo-lit letters. Internally illuminated cabinet (box) wall signs are prohibited.

**(3) Window Signs.**

> \(i\) Window signs shall not exceed twenty-five percent (25%) of the total window area of the window in which they are displayed.
>
> \(ii\) Window signs shall not be illuminated by flashing or animated lighting.

**§245-50(d). Permitted Signs in the B-2 General Business District.** The following sign standards shall apply in the B-2 General Business District:

> \(1\) **Monument Signs.** Each lot with frontage on a public street shall be permitted one (1) monument sign per street frontage, not to exceed two (2) total. The maximum height shall be eight (8) feet, and the maximum sign face area shall be forty-eight (48) square feet per side. Monument signs shall be set back a minimum of five (5) feet from any property line.
>
> \(2\) **Wall Signs.** Each building shall be permitted a maximum of three (3) wall signs. The aggregate sign face area shall not exceed two (2) square feet per linear foot of building frontage. No individual wall sign shall exceed eighty (80) square feet.
>
> \(3\) All other general standards of §245-50(b) shall apply.

**§245-50(e). Permitted Signs in Residential Districts.** In all residential zoning districts (R-1 through R-5), the following signs shall be permitted:

> \(1\) One (1) identification sign per lot, not exceeding four (4) square feet in area, identifying the name and address of the occupant.
>
> \(2\) Permitted nonresidential uses in residential districts (e.g., houses of worship, schools) shall be permitted one (1) freestanding identification sign not exceeding twelve (12) square feet in area and six (6) feet in height, and one (1) wall sign not exceeding twelve (12) square feet.

**§245-50(f). Temporary Signs.** The following temporary signs shall be permitted in all zoning districts, subject to the standards set forth herein:

> \(1\) **Construction Signs.** One (1) construction sign per street frontage, not exceeding thirty-two (32) square feet in area, identifying the project, owner, architect, engineer, and contractor. Construction signs shall be removed within thirty (30) days of the issuance of a certificate of occupancy or completion of construction, whichever occurs first.
>
> \(2\) **Real Estate Signs.** One (1) real estate sign per lot, not exceeding twelve (12) square feet in area, advertising the sale, lease, or rental of the property. Real estate signs shall be removed within seven (7) days of the closing of sale or execution of a lease.
>
> \(3\) **Grand Opening Banners.** One (1) grand opening banner per business, not exceeding thirty-two (32) square feet, displayed for a period not to exceed thirty (30) days. A temporary sign permit is required.

**§245-50(g). Prohibited Signs.** The following signs are prohibited in all zoning districts within the Borough:

> \(1\) Billboards and off-premises advertising signs.
>
> \(2\) Roof signs, including signs mounted on or above any roof surface.
>
> \(3\) Inflatable signs, balloon signs, and tethered aerial signs.
>
> \(4\) Portable signs, including A-frame and sandwich board signs placed within any public right-of-way.
>
> \(5\) Pole signs and pylon signs.
>
> \(6\) Signs affixed to fences, utility poles, trees, or other structures not designed for the display of signs.
>
> \(7\) Signs displayed on vehicles or trailers parked on a lot primarily for the purpose of advertising, rather than for active transportation use.

**§245-50(h). Exempt Signs.** The following signs shall not require a sign permit and shall be exempt from the area, height, and number limitations of this section, provided they comply with the general standards of §245-50(b):

> \(1\) Address numbers and nameplates not exceeding two (2) square feet in area.
>
> \(2\) Governmental, regulatory, traffic, and directional signs erected by or at the direction of a governmental authority.
>
> \(3\) Flags of the United States, the State of New Jersey, the Borough of Maplewood, or any other governmental entity, displayed on a flagpole.
>
> \(4\) Holiday decorations displayed for a period not exceeding forty-five (45) days.
>
> \(5\) Window signs, as regulated by §245-50(c)(3), not exceeding twenty-five percent (25%) of the total window area.

**§245-50(i). Nonconforming Signs.** Any sign that was lawfully erected prior to the adoption or amendment of this section and that does not conform to the current requirements of this section shall be deemed a nonconforming sign. A nonconforming sign may continue to be maintained but shall not be enlarged, relocated, or structurally altered except to bring it into conformity with this section. A nonconforming sign that is destroyed or damaged to the extent of more than fifty percent (50%) of its replacement cost, as determined by the Construction Official, shall not be reconstructed except in full conformity with this section. Any nonconforming sign that is not maintained in good condition, or that is abandoned or associated with a use that has been discontinued for a period of more than ninety (90) days, shall be removed by the property owner within ninety (90) days of receipt of written notice from the Construction Official. Failure to remove such sign within the specified period shall constitute a violation of this chapter and shall be subject to the penalties established in §245-62.

**[ARTICLE X --- GENERAL PROVISIONS (SELECTED EXCERPTS)]{.underline}**

**§245-55. Nonconforming Uses, Structures, and Lots.**

> **(a)** Any use, structure, or lot that lawfully existed on the effective date of this chapter or any amendment thereto but that does not conform to the current requirements of this chapter shall be deemed nonconforming and may continue subject to the limitations of this section and the provisions of N.J.S.A. 40:55D-68. The burden of establishing the lawful nonconforming status of any use, structure, or lot shall be on the property owner.
>
> **(b)** A nonconforming use shall not be expanded, enlarged, or extended to occupy a greater area of land or a greater gross floor area than was occupied on the date the use became nonconforming. A nonconforming use shall not be changed to another nonconforming use.
>
> **(c)** A nonconforming use that is discontinued for a period of twelve (12) consecutive months shall be deemed abandoned, and any subsequent use of the premises shall conform to all requirements of this chapter applicable to the zoning district in which the premises are located. Intent to resume the nonconforming use shall not be sufficient to avoid a finding of abandonment if the use has not been actually conducted on the premises for the requisite twelve-month period.
>
> **(d)** A nonconforming structure may be maintained and repaired but shall not be enlarged, extended, reconstructed, or structurally altered unless the enlargement, extension, reconstruction, or alteration conforms to all current requirements of this chapter. Routine maintenance and repair necessary to keep the structure in a safe and habitable condition shall not be considered an enlargement or structural alteration.
>
> **(e)** Nothing in this section shall be construed to prevent the strengthening or restoration of a nonconforming structure to a safe condition as required or ordered by the Construction Official or any other agency having jurisdiction.

**§245-58. Variances and Appeals.**

> **(a)** The Zoning Board of Adjustment may, in accordance with N.J.S.A. 40:55D-70, grant variances from the strict application of this chapter where the applicant demonstrates the requisite statutory criteria. Specifically:
>
> \(1\) For a subsection (c)(1) \"hardship\" variance, the applicant must demonstrate that by reason of exceptional narrowness, shallowness, or shape of the property, or by reason of exceptional topographic conditions, or by reason of other extraordinary and exceptional conditions affecting the specific piece of property, the strict application of the regulations of this chapter would result in peculiar and exceptional practical difficulties to, or exceptional and undue hardship upon, the owner of the property.
>
> \(2\) For a subsection (c)(2) \"flexible\" or \"benefits/detriments\" variance, the applicant must demonstrate that the purposes of the Municipal Land Use Law (N.J.S.A. 40:55D-2) would be advanced by a deviation from the zoning ordinance requirements, and that the benefits of the deviation would substantially outweigh any detriment. Such variance may be granted, with or without conditions, provided there is no substantial detriment to the public good and the variance will not substantially impair the intent and purpose of the zone plan and zoning ordinance.
>
> **(b)** The Zoning Board of Adjustment may impose reasonable conditions and safeguards upon any variance approval to protect the public health, safety, and welfare and to ensure that the purposes and intent of this chapter are carried out. Such conditions shall be set forth in the Board\'s resolution of approval and shall be binding upon the applicant, the property owner, and all successors and assigns.
>
> **(c)** A variance approval shall expire and become null and void if the authorized construction, alteration, or use is not commenced within one (1) year from the date of the Board\'s resolution of approval, unless the Board specifies a different time period in its resolution, or unless the applicant applies for and is granted an extension of time prior to the expiration date. An extension may be granted for good cause shown, for a period not to exceed one (1) additional year.

**[ARTICLE XI --- ADMINISTRATION AND ENFORCEMENT (SELECTED EXCERPTS)]{.underline}**

**§245-60. Zoning Permits and Certificates of Compliance.**

> **(a)** No building or structure shall be erected, constructed, altered, moved, demolished, or converted to a different use, and no land shall be put to a new use, without a zoning permit issued by the Zoning Officer confirming that the proposed construction, alteration, or use is in conformity with the applicable provisions of this chapter.
>
> **(b)** No building, structure, or land shall be occupied or used, and no change in use shall be commenced, until a certificate of compliance has been issued by the Zoning Officer confirming that the building, structure, or use complies with all applicable provisions of this chapter, including all conditions of any variance approval, conditional use approval, or site plan approval granted by the Planning Board or the Zoning Board of Adjustment. The Zoning Officer shall not issue a certificate of compliance until all conditions of approval have been satisfied or, where applicable, performance guarantees have been posted in accordance with N.J.S.A. 40:55D-53.
>
> **(c)** The Zoning Officer shall maintain records of all zoning permits and certificates of compliance issued under this section and shall make such records available for public inspection during normal business hours at Borough Hall.

**§245-62. Violations and Penalties.**

> **(a)** Any person, firm, corporation, or other entity that violates any provision of this chapter, or any condition of a variance approval, conditional use approval, site plan approval, or subdivision approval, shall be subject to the penalties established by N.J.S.A. 40:55D-18, as amended from time to time. Each and every day that a violation continues after the expiration of a notice to cure or comply shall constitute a separate and distinct offense.
>
> **(b)** The penalties for violation of this chapter shall include a fine of not less than one hundred dollars (\$100.00) and not more than one thousand dollars (\$1,000.00) per offense, or imprisonment in the county jail for a term not exceeding ninety (90) days, or a period of community service not exceeding ninety (90) days, or any combination thereof.
>
> **(c)** In addition to the penalties set forth above, the Borough may institute civil proceedings in the Superior Court of New Jersey to compel compliance with this chapter, including applications for temporary and permanent injunctive relief, and may recover reasonable attorneys\' fees and costs of enforcement as permitted by law.

**CERTIFICATION**

The foregoing excerpts have been compiled from the official Maplewood Municipal Zoning Ordinance, Chapter 245, as codified in the Borough Code and as amended through Ordinance No. 2024-19 (adopted by the Mayor and Council of the Borough of Maplewood on August 12, 2024; effective September 1, 2024). These excerpts are certified as a true and accurate reproduction of the relevant sections of the official ordinance on file with the Office of the Borough Clerk, Borough of Maplewood, Essex County, New Jersey.
