**BOROUGH OF MAPLEWOOD**

**ZONING BOARD OF ADJUSTMENT**

**COUNTY OF ESSEX, STATE OF NEW JERSEY**

**RESOLUTION NO. ZB-2013-22**

**ADOPTED: June 14, 2013**

**IN THE MATTER OF THE APPLICATION OF MAPLEWOOD GATEWAY ASSOCIATES LP FOR BULK VARIANCE RELIEF PURSUANT TO N.J.S.A. 40:55D-70(c) --- PROPERTY: 1875 CRESCENT BOULEVARD, BLOCK 412, LOT 17**

**[SECTION 1 --- RECITALS]{.underline}**

**WHEREAS**, the following facts have been presented to and considered by the Zoning Board of Adjustment of the Borough of Maplewood, County of Essex, State of New Jersey (hereinafter, the \"Board\"):

1\. **WHEREAS**, the applicant in this matter is Maplewood Gateway Associates LP, a limited partnership organized and existing under the laws of the State of New Jersey, with its principal place of business located in Maplewood, New Jersey (hereinafter, the \"Applicant\"). Lorraine DiMartino serves as the General Partner of Maplewood Gateway Associates LP, and appeared before the Board on behalf of the partnership in connection with this application; and

2\. **WHEREAS**, the Applicant is the owner of certain real property located at 1875 Crescent Boulevard, Maplewood, New Jersey 07040, designated as Block 412, Lot 17 on the Official Tax Map of the Borough of Maplewood, County of Essex, State of New Jersey (hereinafter, the \"Property\" or the \"Subject Property\"); and

3\. **WHEREAS**, the Subject Property is located within the B-3 Mixed-Use Business District, as established and defined by the Maplewood Municipal Zoning Ordinance, Chapter 245 of the Code of the Borough of Maplewood; and

4\. **WHEREAS**, the Subject Property has a total lot area of approximately 4.2 acres, equating to approximately 182,952 square feet, as depicted on the survey submitted in connection with this application; and

5\. **WHEREAS**, the Applicant proposes to construct a single-story commercial warehouse/flex building, designated as \"Building B,\" with a footprint of approximately 18,500 square feet on the eastern portion of the Subject Property, in conjunction with a three-story mixed-use structure, designated as \"Building A,\" with a footprint of approximately 14,000 square feet to be situated on the western portion of the Subject Property. Building A is intended to contain ground-floor retail space with residential dwelling units on the upper two floors, while Building B is intended to accommodate warehouse, distribution, and flexible commercial space uses; and

6\. **WHEREAS**, the eastern boundary of the Subject Property directly abuts a zone classified as R-4 Residential under the Maplewood Municipal Zoning Ordinance, and the residential properties along that boundary consist primarily of single-family detached dwellings; and

7\. **WHEREAS**, pursuant to §245-18 of the Maplewood Municipal Zoning Ordinance, the minimum side yard setback for properties located within the B-3 Mixed-Use Business District that abut a residential zone is twenty-five (25) feet. This increased setback requirement is intended to provide an adequate transition and buffer between commercial and residential uses; and

8\. **WHEREAS**, the proposed Building B, as depicted on the site plans and architectural drawings submitted in connection with this application and prepared by Meridian Design Group, dated February 15, 2013, last revised April 10, 2013, would be situated approximately eighteen (18) feet from the eastern property boundary, resulting in a deficiency of seven (7) feet from the required twenty-five (25) foot residential buffer setback; and

9\. **WHEREAS**, the Applicant therefore requires bulk variance relief pursuant to N.J.S.A. 40:55D-70(c) to permit a side yard setback of eighteen (18) feet where twenty-five (25) feet is required under §245-18 of the Maplewood Municipal Zoning Ordinance; and

10\. **WHEREAS**, the application for bulk variance relief was filed with the Board on March 22, 2013, and was duly noticed to all property owners within two hundred (200) feet of the Subject Property, as required by N.J.S.A. 40:55D-12. Publication of the required legal notice was made in the *Maplewood-South Orange News-Record* on April 4, 2013 and April 11, 2013, and proof of service and publication were submitted to the Board and found to be in compliance with all statutory requirements; and

11\. **WHEREAS**, a public hearing on this application was conducted before the Board on May 8, 2013, and was continued to June 14, 2013, at which sessions the Applicant presented testimony from Robert Castillo, PP, AICP, a licensed professional planner with the firm of Castillo Planning Associates, and from Angela Ferraro, PE, a licensed professional engineer with the firm of Eastpointe Engineering LLC. Both witnesses were accepted by the Board as experts in their respective fields, and their testimony, together with all documentary exhibits, was received into evidence; and

12\. **WHEREAS**, members of the public were afforded the opportunity to comment at both hearing sessions in accordance with the requirements of the Municipal Land Use Law. Five (5) members of the public appeared in opposition to the application, raising concerns regarding visual screening of the proposed warehouse building from the adjacent residential properties, potential noise from warehouse operations and truck movements, and increased traffic on Crescent Boulevard and on the local residential streets in the vicinity of the Subject Property. The Board has carefully considered all testimony and evidence presented, including the objections and concerns raised by members of the public.

**[SECTION 2 --- FINDINGS OF FACT]{.underline}**

Based upon the testimony presented, the evidence submitted, the documents entered into the record, and the deliberations of the Board, the Maplewood Zoning Board of Adjustment hereby makes the following findings of fact:

1\. The Applicant demonstrated that strict application of the twenty-five (25) foot side yard setback requirement of §245-18 of the Maplewood Municipal Zoning Ordinance would create an undue hardship by rendering the eastern portion of the Subject Property effectively unusable for the proposed warehouse/flex building, given the irregular configuration of the lot along its eastern boundary, the location of existing utility easements traversing the central portion of the property, and the necessary placement of Building A on the western portion of the lot to achieve the setbacks required from Crescent Boulevard. The Applicant\'s professional planner credibly testified that compliance with the full twenty-five (25) foot setback would reduce the buildable envelope for Building B to such a degree that the structure could not be designed to a size sufficient to be economically viable. The Board finds this testimony credible and persuasive.

2\. The Board finds that the requested variance can be granted without substantial detriment to the public good and without substantially impairing the intent and purpose of the zone plan and the zoning ordinance of the Borough of Maplewood, provided that adequate buffering and screening is installed along the entire eastern boundary of the Subject Property to mitigate the reduced setback\'s impact on the adjacent residential properties. The Board has carefully weighed the potential impact on the neighboring R-4 Residential zone and concludes that the conditions imposed herein will adequately protect the health, safety, and welfare of the neighboring residents.

3\. The benefits of granting the requested variance --- including the economic utilization of the Subject Property consistent with the purposes of the B-3 Mixed-Use Business District, the generation of an increased tax ratable for the Borough of Maplewood, and the creation of employment opportunities within the Borough --- outweigh the detriments associated with the reduction of the side yard setback from twenty-five (25) feet to eighteen (18) feet along the eastern boundary abutting the residential zone, particularly in light of the conditions of approval imposed herein. The Board further notes that the Applicant\'s professional planner testified without contradiction that the proposed development is consistent with the goals and objectives of the 2010 Maplewood Master Plan, which encourages mixed-use development and economic revitalization within the B-3 district.

4\. The proposed Building B will be a single-story structure with a maximum height of approximately twenty-two (22) feet, as measured from the finished grade to the highest point of the roof structure. This height is substantially below the forty-five (45) foot and three (3) story maximum height permitted in the B-3 district under §245-16 of the Zoning Ordinance. The Board finds that the reduced height of the building will significantly mitigate the visual impact of the reduced setback on the adjacent residential zone, and that the building will not create an overbearing or oppressive visual presence when viewed from the neighboring residential properties.

5\. The Board notes that the proposed warehouse/flex use is classified as a conditional use in the B-3 Mixed-Use Business District pursuant to §245-15(c)(3) of the Maplewood Municipal Zoning Ordinance, and that the Applicant has indicated its intention to seek, or will be required to obtain, separate conditional use approval from the Maplewood Planning Board in connection with that use. This variance relief is strictly limited to the bulk standard governing the side yard setback along the eastern property boundary and does not constitute, and shall not be construed as, conditional use approval, site plan approval, or any other form of land use approval other than the specific bulk variance described herein.

**[SECTION 3 --- CONDITIONS OF APPROVAL]{.underline}**

**NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED** that the Maplewood Zoning Board of Adjustment hereby grants to the Applicant, Maplewood Gateway Associates LP, the requested bulk variance relief to permit a side yard setback of eighteen (18) feet along the eastern property boundary where twenty-five (25) feet is required pursuant to §245-18 of the Maplewood Municipal Zoning Ordinance, subject to strict compliance with each and all of the following conditions:

**Condition 1 --- Landscape Buffer.** The Applicant shall install and perpetually maintain a fifteen (15) foot wide evergreen landscape buffer along the entire eastern property boundary abutting the R-4 Residential zone. Said buffer shall consist of a minimum of one (1) evergreen tree per eight (8) linear feet of boundary, with a minimum planting height of six (6) feet at the time of installation, supplemented by evergreen shrubs planted in staggered rows to create a continuous visual screen achieving a minimum opacity of seventy-five percent (75%) within two (2) growing seasons of installation. The landscape plan shall be prepared by a licensed landscape architect and shall be submitted to the Borough Zoning Officer for review and approval prior to the issuance of a Certificate of Occupancy for Building B. All plantings shall be maintained in a healthy and living condition, and any dead, diseased, or damaged plantings shall be replaced by the property owner within one (1) planting season of the date on which the Zoning Officer provides written notice of such deficiency.

**Condition 2 --- Operating Hours.** The warehouse/flex use in Building B shall be limited to the following hours of operation: 7:00 AM to 9:00 PM, Monday through Saturday. No warehouse or flex-space operations, including but not limited to deliveries, loading, unloading, truck movements, forklift operations, and any activities generating noise perceptible at the property boundary, shall occur on Sundays or federal holidays. The Applicant shall post and maintain a sign in a conspicuous location at each loading dock and entrance to Building B stating the permitted hours of operation.

**Condition 3 --- Outdoor Storage Prohibition.** No outdoor storage of materials, equipment, goods, products, pallets, containers, dumpsters, roll-off containers, or any other items shall be permitted on any portion of the Subject Property. All storage associated with the warehouse/flex use shall be fully enclosed within Building B at all times. Temporary placement of materials or goods outside of the building in connection with loading or unloading operations shall be limited to the period during which such loading or unloading is actively occurring, and in no event shall any materials remain outside the building for a period exceeding two (2) hours.

**Condition 4 --- Compliance with All Other Ordinance Requirements.** The Applicant shall comply with all other applicable provisions of the Maplewood Municipal Zoning Ordinance, Chapter 245 of the Code of the Borough of Maplewood, including but not limited to the requirements governing parking, signage, stormwater management, lighting, refuse collection, and site maintenance. Nothing in this Resolution shall be construed as a waiver or variance from any ordinance requirement other than the specific side yard setback variance granted herein.

**Condition 5 --- Approval of Other Agencies.** The Applicant shall obtain all other required approvals from all agencies having jurisdiction over the proposed development, including but not limited to site plan approval from the Maplewood Planning Board, conditional use approval for the warehouse/flex use from the Maplewood Planning Board, approval from the Essex County Planning Board, soil erosion and sediment control certification from the Essex County Soil Conservation District, approval from the New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection (if applicable), and all applicable construction permits and certificates of occupancy from the Borough of Maplewood Construction Official.

**[SECTION 4 --- TRANSFERABILITY LIMITATION]{.underline}**

**BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED** that this variance approval is personal to the Applicant, Maplewood Gateway Associates LP, and its principals. This variance shall expire automatically upon the occurrence of any of the following events: (a) the approved use is discontinued for a period of twelve (12) consecutive months; or (b) the property is transferred, conveyed, assigned, or otherwise alienated to any person or entity other than the Applicant, whether by sale, lease of the entire premises, foreclosure, or operation of law, UNLESS the successor owner, transferee, or assignee files an application with this Board for confirmation of the variance within ninety (90) days of the date of transfer. Failure to file such application within the ninety (90) day period shall result in the automatic expiration of this variance, and the property shall thereafter be required to comply with the full setback requirements of §245-18 of the Maplewood Municipal Zoning Ordinance. The Board reserves the right, upon any such confirmation application, to impose additional or modified conditions as it deems appropriate in light of changed circumstances.

**[SECTION 5 --- VOTING RECORD]{.underline}**

The foregoing Resolution was adopted by the Maplewood Zoning Board of Adjustment at its regular meeting of June 14, 2013, by the following roll call vote:

  David Greenwald         Member                  AYE

  Margaret Hsu            Member (Alternate 1)    RECUSED --- did not participate
  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Vote: 5 AYES, 1 NAY, 1 RECUSED. Motion carries.**

The Resolution is hereby adopted and shall take effect immediately upon memorialization and filing.

**[ALTA/NSPS LAND TITLE SURVEY --- NARRATIVE SUMMARY AND DATA TABLES]{.underline}**

**Prepared in Connection with the Proposed Acquisition of 1875 Crescent Boulevard, Maplewood, New Jersey 07040**

Survey Prepared by: **Cartwright Surveying Associates** Thomas Cartwright, PLS New Jersey Professional Land Surveyor License No. 38742 14 Commerce Drive, Suite 200, Morristown, New Jersey 07960

**Date of Survey: February 28, 2025** Date of Last Field Revision: February 28, 2025

**Prepared For:**

> **Ridgeline Title & Escrow LLC** (Title Company) 42 Park Place, Suite 1100, Newark, New Jersey 07102
>
> **Briarcliff National Bank** (Buyer\'s Lender) 300 Main Street, Briarcliff Manor, New York 10510

**Additional Distribution:**

> Holloway Stern LLP (Buyer\'s Counsel) Crescent Boulevard Holdings LLC (Buyer SPV)

**Reference Standard:** This survey has been prepared in accordance with the 2021 Minimum Standard Detail Requirements for ALTA/NSPS Land Title Surveys, as jointly adopted and promulgated by the American Land Title Association and the National Society of Professional Surveyors, including the following optional Table A items: Items 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6(a), 6(b), 8, 9, 11(a), 11(b), 13, 16, 17, 18, and 19.

**[Section 1: Property Identification]{.underline}**

**Property Address:** 1875 Crescent Boulevard, Maplewood, New Jersey 07040

**Tax Identification:** Block 412, Lot 17 on the Official Tax Map of the Borough of Maplewood, Essex County, New Jersey.

**Current Owner of Record:** Maplewood Gateway Associates LP, a New Jersey limited partnership, as set forth in that certain Bargain and Sale Deed recorded on August 12, 2013, in the Office of the Essex County Clerk in Deed Book 9847 at Page 312, Instrument No. 2013-054271.

**Zoning District:** The subject property is classified within the **B-3 Mixed-Use Business District** as shown on the Official Zoning Map of the Borough of Maplewood, as most recently amended.

**Adjacent Zoning Districts:** The property is bordered by the following zoning districts: **R-4 Residential** (north and east), **B-2 General Business** (west), and **B-3 Mixed-Use Business** (south, across Crescent Boulevard).

**Variance Reference:** The surveyor was provided a copy of **Resolution No. ZB-2013-22**, dated June 14, 2013, issued by the Maplewood Zoning Board of Adjustment, which granted a variance for a reduced east side yard setback for the subject property. This resolution is referenced on the accompanying survey plat.

**Surveyor\'s Note:** Variance Resolution No. ZB-2013-22 (June 14, 2013) was provided by the property owner and is referenced hereon. The resolution contains a condition stating the variance is personal to the applicant and may expire upon transfer of ownership. Surveyor makes no determination as to the current legal status or transferability of said variance. Interested parties should consult legal counsel regarding the continuing validity of the variance in connection with any contemplated conveyance of the property.

**[Section 2: Lot Dimensions and Area]{.underline}**

**Total Lot Area:** 182,952 square feet (4.200 acres), computed by coordinate geometry from field-established boundary points and confirmed against recorded deed descriptions.

**Lot Width:** 312.00 feet, measured along the Crescent Boulevard frontage at the building setback line.

**Lot Depth:** 587.00 feet, measured along the east property line, perpendicular to the northerly right-of-way line of Crescent Boulevard.

**Boundary Description:** The subject property is bounded on the south by Crescent Boulevard (a 60-foot public right-of-way); on the west by Lot 18, Block 412; on the north by Lots 5 and 6, Block 413 (R-4 Residential zone); and on the east by Lot 16, Block 412 (R-4 Residential zone).

**Metes and Bounds Summary (Abbreviated):** Beginning at the intersection of the northerly right-of-way line of Crescent Boulevard with the easterly property line of the subject premises, said point being marked by a concrete monument found; thence running (1) North 02°15\'30\" West along the easterly property line, a distance of 587.00 feet to an iron pipe found at the northeast corner; thence (2) South 87°44\'30\" West along the northerly property line, a distance of 312.00 feet to an iron pipe found at the northwest corner; thence (3) South 02°15\'30\" East along the westerly property line, a distance of 587.00 feet to an iron pipe found at the southwest corner on the northerly right-of-way line of Crescent Boulevard; thence (4) North 87°44\'30\" East along said northerly right-of-way line of Crescent Boulevard, a distance of 312.00 feet to the point and place of beginning.

**Monuments Found:** Iron pipes were found at all four property corners. A concrete monument was found at the southeast corner at the Crescent Boulevard right-of-way intersection. All monuments are in good condition and undisturbed.

**[Section 3: Improvements --- Buildings]{.underline}**

**3.1 Building A --- Mixed-Use Structure**

**Description:** Three-story mixed-use structure containing ground-floor retail space and upper-floor office space. The building is oriented with its primary facade facing south toward Crescent Boulevard.

**Footprint Area:** 14,000 square feet.

**Gross Floor Area:** 42,000 square feet (three stories at approximately 14,000 square feet per floor).

**Building Height:** 44 feet, measured from average finished grade at the building perimeter to the highest point of the roof structure (parapet cap).

**Number of Stories:** Three (3).

**Construction:** Steel frame with masonry veneer exterior walls and a flat built-up roof with parapet. The building is served by a central HVAC system with rooftop mechanical equipment observed behind the parapet.

**Year Built:** 2014, per Borough of Maplewood municipal construction records.

**Ground Floor Elevation:** 44.5 feet NAVD88, measured at the main entrance threshold on the south (Crescent Boulevard) facade.

**Signage Observed:** A freestanding monument sign is located at the Crescent Boulevard frontage, immediately east of the primary curb cut (Curb Cut No. 1). The monument sign has a measured height of 8 feet and a sign face area of approximately 48 square feet (double-faced). Three (3) wall-mounted tenant identification signs were observed on the Crescent Boulevard (south) facade of Building A, each approximately 20 square feet in area.

**3.2 Building B --- Warehouse/Flex Space**

**Description:** Single-story commercial warehouse and flex space building located in the northern portion of the site, behind and to the north of Building A.

**Footprint Area:** 18,500 square feet.

**Gross Floor Area:** 18,500 square feet (single story).

**Building Height:** 22 feet, measured from average finished grade at the building perimeter to the highest point of the roof.

**Number of Stories:** One (1).

**Construction:** Pre-engineered metal building with concrete slab on grade. Metal panel exterior cladding on all four facades.

**Year Built:** 2014, per Borough of Maplewood municipal construction records.

**Signage Observed:** One (1) wall-mounted sign on the south-facing (parking lot side) facade, approximately 32 square feet in area.

**Loading and Access Features:** One overhead door (12 feet wide by 14 feet high) was observed on the west facade of Building B. One at-grade loading dock and apron area was noted on the north side of Building B, facing the rear (north) property boundary and the R-4 Residential zone. The loading dock apron area measures approximately 40 feet by 25 feet. No screening wall, fence, or landscape screening structures were observed surrounding or adjacent to the loading dock area at the time of the field survey.

**[Section 4: Setback Measurements]{.underline}**

The following table summarizes the measured building setbacks from each property boundary, compared against the applicable requirements of the Maplewood Municipal Zoning Ordinance for the B-3 Mixed-Use Business District:

  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Setback Location**   **Direction**           **Adjacent Zone**      **Required Setback (per Ordinance)**   **Measured Setback**   **Applicable Building**   **Notes**
  ---------------------- ----------------------- ---------------------- -------------------------------------- ---------------------- ------------------------- ------------
  Front Yard             South (Crescent Blvd)   B-3 (across street)    20 ft min.                             22.0 ft                Building A                Compliant

  Side Yard (West)       West                    B-2 General Business   15 ft min.                             16.0 ft                Building B                Compliant

  Side Yard (East)       East                    R-4 Residential        25 ft min. (residential buffer)        19.0 ft                Building B                See Note 1

  Rear Yard (North)      North                   R-4 Residential        35 ft min. (residential buffer)        28.0 ft                Building A                See Note 2
  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Note 1 --- East Side Yard:** Variance Resolution No. ZB-2013-22, issued by the Maplewood Zoning Board of Adjustment on June 14, 2013, approved a reduction of the east side yard setback to 18 feet. The measured setback of 19.0 feet exceeds the variance-approved minimum of 18 feet. However, the standard B-3 requirement when abutting an R-4 Residential zone is 25 feet. As noted in Section 1 and Section 10.1 of this summary, the variance resolution contains a condition regarding transferability upon change of ownership. See the surveyor\'s note regarding the transferability of the variance.

**Note 2 --- Rear Yard (North):** The north boundary abuts Lots 5 and 6, Block 413, which are classified R-4 Residential on the Official Zoning Map. Per Section 245-18 of the Maplewood Municipal Zoning Ordinance, the minimum rear yard setback for properties in the B-3 district when abutting a residential zone is 35 feet (residential buffer requirement). The measured setback of 28.0 feet from the north face of Building A to the north property line is 7.0 feet less than the residential buffer requirement. No variance or other land use approval for this setback reduction was provided to the surveyor, and no such approval was identified in the title commitment documents furnished to the surveyor for this engagement.

**[Section 5: Coverage and Intensity Calculations]{.underline}**

  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Category**                 **Computation**           **Value**       **Maximum Permitted**   **Status**
  ---------------------------- ------------------------- --------------- ----------------------- --------------
  **Building Coverage**                                                                          

  Building A Footprint         ---                       14,000 SF       ---                     ---

  Building B Footprint         ---                       18,500 SF       ---                     ---

  Total Building Coverage      14,000 + 18,500           **32,500 SF**   ---                     ---

  Building Coverage Ratio      32,500 / 182,952          **17.77%**      35%                     Compliant

  **Impervious Coverage**                                                                        

  Buildings                    ---                       32,500 SF       ---                     ---

  Parking Areas & Driveways    ---                       56,100 SF       ---                     ---

  Walkways, Patios & Other     ---                       8,200 SF        ---                     ---

  Total Impervious Coverage    32,500 + 56,100 + 8,200   **96,800 SF**   ---                     ---

  Impervious Coverage Ratio    96,800 / 182,952          **52.91%**      75%                     Compliant

  **Floor Area Ratio (FAR)**                                                                     

  Building A GFA               ---                       42,000 SF       ---                     ---

  Building B GFA               ---                       18,500 SF       ---                     ---

  Total GFA                    42,000 + 18,500           **60,500 SF**   ---                     ---

  FAR                          60,500 / 182,952          **0.3307**      1.50                    Compliant
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

All coverage and intensity calculations are based on field-measured building footprint areas and impervious surface areas as observed during the field survey conducted February 22--24, 2025. Gross floor area figures are computed from measured footprint areas multiplied by the number of stories for each building.

**[Section 6: Parking and Access]{.underline}**

**Surface Parking:** A total of **187 striped parking spaces** were observed and counted within the site\'s surface parking areas, including 8 ADA-accessible spaces located near the main entrance to Building A. The parking areas are paved with bituminous asphalt and are included in the impervious coverage calculation set forth in Section 5 (56,100 SF for parking areas and driveways combined).

**Access Points:**

> **Curb Cut No. 1:** Located on Crescent Boulevard, approximately 80 feet east of the western property line. Driveway apron is 30 feet wide and provides two-way vehicular access to the primary parking area serving Building A.
>
> **Curb Cut No. 2:** Located on Crescent Boulevard, approximately 220 feet east of the western property line. Driveway apron is 24 feet wide and provides two-way vehicular access to the eastern portion of the parking area.
>
> **Curb Cut No. 3:** Located on Elm Terrace (rear/north side of the property), accessed via a 20-foot wide driveway at the northwest corner of the property. Elm Terrace is a local residential street within the R-4 Residential zone. This curb cut provides access primarily to the Building B loading area and the rear parking area.

**Loading Dock:** One at-grade loading dock and apron area was observed on the north side of Building B, measuring approximately 40 feet by 25 feet, oriented toward the rear (north) property boundary and the R-4 Residential zone beyond. No screening wall, fence, or landscape screening was observed around the loading dock area at the time of the field survey.

**[Section 7: Landscape Buffer --- Eastern Boundary]{.underline}**

The surveyor observed a landscape planting strip along the entire eastern property boundary, which constitutes the boundary abutting the R-4 Residential zone (Lot 16, Block 412).

**Measured Width of Landscape Strip:** The buffer width was measured at three representative cross-sections along the eastern boundary:

> • North end: 11.8 feet
>
> • Mid-point: 12.2 feet
>
> • South end: 12.0 feet
>
> • **Average width: 12.0 feet**

**Planting Composition Observed:** The plantings within the buffer strip consist of sparse deciduous trees and shrubs, predominantly maple (*Acer* spp.) and ornamental cherry (*Prunus* spp.). No evergreen species were identified along the buffer at the time of the field survey.

**Ground Cover:** Mixed turf grass and bare soil patches were observed. No continuous ground cover planting was present within the buffer area.

**Fencing:** No fencing was observed along the eastern property boundary.

**Surveyor\'s Note:** The variance approval resolution (ZB-2013-22) provided to the surveyor requires a 15-foot evergreen landscape buffer along the entire eastern property boundary as a condition of the reduced east side yard setback approval. The measured buffer width of 12.0 feet is 3.0 feet less than the required 15.0 feet. Additionally, the plantings observed within the buffer are predominantly deciduous rather than evergreen. The surveyor makes no determination as to compliance with variance conditions; however, these observations are noted for the benefit of the client and title company. Parties should review the variance conditions in consultation with legal counsel and, if appropriate, the Borough zoning enforcement officer.

**[Section 8: Flood Zone and Environmental Notations]{.underline}**

**FEMA Flood Insurance Rate Map (FIRM) Reference:** Panel No. 34013C0042F, effective date December 4, 2020, as published by the Federal Emergency Management Agency.

**Flood Zone Determination:** The northeastern corner of the subject property, encompassing approximately **0.3 acres (13,068 square feet)**, lies within **FEMA Flood Zone AE** (Special Flood Hazard Area --- 100-year floodplain). The **Base Flood Elevation (BFE) is 42.0 feet NAVD88** as depicted on the effective FIRM panel.

**Extent of Zone AE Area:** The Zone AE area extends from the northeast corner of the lot inward approximately 75 feet along the north property boundary and approximately 175 feet along the east property boundary, forming an irregular triangular shape. The Zone AE area is currently undeveloped, covered by turf grass and a portion of the rear parking area. No buildings or other significant structures are located within the Zone AE area.

**Building Elevations Relative to BFE:** The Building A ground floor elevation of 44.5 feet NAVD88 is 2.5 feet above the BFE of 42.0 feet NAVD88. The Zone AE boundary does not encroach upon the footprint of either Building A or Building B.

**Remainder of Property:** The balance of the subject property, outside of the Zone AE area described above, is located within **FEMA Zone X** (areas of minimal flood hazard).

**Surveyor\'s Note:** Approximately 0.3 acres (13,068 square feet) of the subject property in the northeast corner is located within FEMA Flood Zone AE with a Base Flood Elevation of 42.0 feet NAVD88. Future development, grading, filling, or construction of improvements within this area may be subject to local floodplain development regulations, NJDEP flood hazard area control requirements, and FEMA permitting requirements. The existing Building A finished floor elevation of 44.5 feet NAVD88 is 2.5 feet above the BFE. Parties contemplating any future development or modification of improvements in the northeast portion of the site should consult with the Borough of Maplewood Construction Official and the New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection regarding applicable flood hazard area regulations.

**[Section 9: Easements and Encumbrances]{.underline}**

The following easements and encumbrances were identified from the title commitment documents furnished to the surveyor and from field observations:

**Utility Easements:**

> 1\. A 10-foot wide utility easement along the entire southern property boundary (Crescent Boulevard frontage) in favor of Public Service Electric and Gas Company (PSE&G) for underground electric and gas service. Recorded in the Office of the Essex County Clerk in Deed Book 8412 at Page 77, Instrument No. 1998-021344.
>
> 2\. An 8-foot wide sanitary sewer easement running north-south along the western property boundary in favor of the Borough of Maplewood for municipal sanitary sewer infrastructure. Recorded in Deed Book 7956 at Page 203, Instrument No. 1995-009821.
>
> 3\. A 15-foot wide drainage easement in the northeast corner of the property in favor of the Essex County Flood Control and Drainage Authority for stormwater management and drainage purposes. Recorded in Deed Book 9102 at Page 415, Instrument No. 2006-038712. This drainage easement overlaps with the FEMA Zone AE area described in Section 8 and further constrains development activity in the northeast corner of the property.

**Encroachments:** No encroachments of buildings, structures, or other improvements into any easement area were observed during the field survey.

**Party Walls / Shared Access:** None observed.

**Rights-of-Way:** Crescent Boulevard (60-foot right-of-way, publicly dedicated); Elm Terrace (40-foot right-of-way, publicly dedicated).

**[Section 10: Surveyor\'s Notes and Certifications]{.underline}**

**10.1 General Notes**

1\. This survey was performed in accordance with the 2021 ALTA/NSPS Minimum Standard Detail Requirements for Land Title Surveys, including the optional Table A items identified on the title page of this summary.

2\. Field work was completed on February 22--24, 2025. This survey is dated **February 28, 2025**.

3\. **Horizontal Datum:** North American Datum of 1983 (NAD83), 2011 adjustment, New Jersey State Plane Coordinate System, East Zone. **Vertical Datum:** North American Vertical Datum of 1988 (NAVD88).

4\. All measurements are reported to the nearest 0.1 foot unless otherwise noted. Angular measurements are reported to the nearest second of arc.

5\. Improvements shown on the survey plat are based on field observations made during the dates of field work. Underground utilities are shown based on visible surface features, utility locate markings provided by NJ One-Call, and available as-built records furnished by the Borough of Maplewood Engineering Department. No excavation was performed to verify underground utility locations or depths.

6\. Flood zone determination is based on the FEMA FIRM panel referenced in Section 8 of this summary. Flood zone boundaries were interpolated from the effective FIRM and scaled to the survey base map.

7\. Zoning information shown hereon is based on the Maplewood Municipal Zoning Ordinance as amended through **Ordinance No. 2024-19** (effective September 1, 2024) and the Official Zoning Map of the Borough of Maplewood.

8\. Variance Resolution No. ZB-2013-22, provided by the property owner, was referenced for setback analysis along the east side yard. Surveyor notes that the resolution contains a condition limiting transferability of the variance; parties should consult legal counsel regarding the effect of any change in ownership on the variance approval and the continued validity of the reduced setback authorized thereunder.

9\. The surveyor\'s observations regarding the eastern boundary landscape buffer set forth in Section 7 are factual field observations only and do not constitute a determination of compliance or noncompliance with any land use approval, variance condition, or municipal ordinance.

**10.2 Certification.** To: Crescent Boulevard Holdings LLC, a Delaware limited liability company; Ridgeline Title & Escrow LLC; Briarcliff National Bank; and Holloway Stern LLP.

I, Thomas Cartwright, PLS, a Professional Land Surveyor duly licensed in the State of New Jersey, do hereby certify that this survey was prepared under my direct supervision and responsible charge, and that it meets or exceeds the 2021 Minimum Standard Detail Requirements for ALTA/NSPS Land Title Surveys as jointly adopted by the American Land Title Association and the National Society of Professional Surveyors, including the optional Table A items identified herein.

This survey accurately depicts the boundaries, improvements, easements, rights-of-way, and other matters shown hereon based on field observations, recorded documents, and other data referenced herein, as of the dates of field work set forth above. This certification is made for the exclusive benefit of the parties named above and their respective successors and assigns in interest to the subject property.

CARTWRIGHT SURVEYING ASSOCIATES

**[PHASE I ENVIRONMENTAL SITE ASSESSMENT]{.underline}**

**[EXECUTIVE SUMMARY]{.underline}**

\ 

**1875 Crescent Boulevard, Maplewood, New Jersey 07040** **Block 412, Lot 17**

\ 

**Prepared for:** Crescent Boulevard Holdings LLC (a Delaware limited liability company) c/o Redfield Capital Partners LLC

Attention: Jonathan Kessler, Managing Partner

\ 

**Prepared by:** Greystone Environmental Consulting LLC 14 Commerce Drive, Suite 200 Morristown, New Jersey 07960

\ 

**Author:** Dr. Anita Rourke, PG, LSRP, Principal

\ 

**Greystone Project No.: GEC-2025-0147**

\ 

**March 15, 2025**

\ 

This Executive Summary is extracted from the full Phase I Environmental Site Assessment report prepared in accordance with ASTM E1527-21. The complete report, including all appendices and supporting documentation, should be referenced for full findings, detailed analysis, and supporting documentation. This Executive Summary does not constitute the complete Phase I ESA and should not be relied upon independently of the full report.

**[1. Purpose and Scope]{.underline}**

Greystone Environmental Consulting LLC (\"Greystone\") was retained by Crescent Boulevard Holdings LLC (the \"User\"), a wholly owned subsidiary of Redfield Capital Partners LLC, to conduct a Phase I Environmental Site Assessment (\"Phase I ESA\") of the property located at 1875 Crescent Boulevard, Maplewood, New Jersey 07040, identified as Block 412, Lot 17 on the Borough of Maplewood tax maps, Essex County, New Jersey (the \"subject property\" or \"Property\"). This assessment was performed in connection with the proposed acquisition of the Property by the User from Maplewood Gateway Associates LP for a purchase price of Eighteen Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$18,500,000).

The Phase I ESA was conducted in accordance with ASTM E1527-21, \"Standard Practice for Environmental Site Assessments: Phase I Environmental Site Assessment Process.\" The purpose of this assessment is to identify Recognized Environmental Conditions (\"RECs\"), Controlled Recognized Environmental Conditions (\"CRECs\"), and Historical Recognized Environmental Conditions (\"HRECs\") in connection with the subject property, consistent with the scope and limitations established by ASTM E1527-21.

This assessment is intended to satisfy the \"All Appropriate Inquiries\" (\"AAI\") standard codified at 40 C.F.R. Part 312, as required for qualification for the innocent landowner defense, contiguous property owner defense, and bona fide prospective purchaser defense to liability under the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act (\"CERCLA\"), 42 U.S.C. § 9601 et seq. The User\'s lender, Briarcliff National Bank, also required the completion of this Phase I ESA as a condition of loan underwriting for the proposed acquisition.

The scope of work for this Phase I ESA included the following components: (i) review of standard federal, state, tribal, and local environmental databases through a regulatory database search report; (ii) historical use review through examination of aerial photographs, Sanborn fire insurance maps, and city directories; (iii) site reconnaissance conducted on February 27, 2025; (iv) interviews with current owner and operator representatives; and (v) evaluation of adjacent and adjoining properties for conditions that may have environmental implications for the subject property. In addition, Greystone reviewed the User questionnaire completed by Jonathan Kessler on behalf of the User, dated February 10, 2025, which provided information regarding the User\'s knowledge of the Property and the intended use following acquisition.

**[2. Property Description]{.underline}**

**Address:** 1875 Crescent Boulevard, Maplewood, New Jersey 07040

**Tax Identification:** Block 412, Lot 17, Borough of Maplewood, Essex County, New Jersey

**Total Lot Area:** Approximately 4.2 acres (182,952 square feet), as determined by reference to the ALTA/NSPS Land Title Survey prepared by Cartwright Surveying Associates, dated February 28, 2025 (prepared under the supervision of Thomas Cartwright, PLS).

**Current Zoning:** B-3 Mixed-Use Business District, Borough of Maplewood. Adjacent zoning designations include R-4 Residential to the north and east, B-2 General Business to the west, and B-3 Mixed-Use Business to the south (across Crescent Boulevard).

**Current Improvements:** The subject property is improved with two principal structures and associated site improvements, as follows:

> • **Building A:** A three-story mixed-use structure containing ground-floor retail space and upper-floor professional office space, comprising approximately 42,000 square feet of gross floor area. Building A was constructed in 2014.
>
> • **Building B:** A single-story commercial warehouse and flex space building, comprising approximately 18,500 square feet of gross floor area. Building B was also constructed in 2014.
>
> • **Surface Parking:** An asphalt surface parking lot containing 187 striped parking spaces, served by two curb cuts on Crescent Boulevard and one curb cut on Elm Terrace to the rear (north) of the Property.

The total gross floor area of existing improvements is approximately 60,500 square feet. Impervious coverage totals approximately 96,800 square feet (52.91% of lot area), consisting of building footprints (approximately 32,500 square feet), parking areas and drives (approximately 56,100 square feet), and walkways and patios (approximately 8,200 square feet).

**Current Owner:** Maplewood Gateway Associates LP (Lorraine DiMartino, General Partner), which acquired the Property in 2011 for \$9,200,000 and developed the current improvements during the 2013--2014 construction period.

**Topography and Drainage:** The Property is generally flat with a gentle slope from the southwest to the northeast. Stormwater drainage flows in a northeasterly direction toward the rear of the Property. The northeastern corner of the site is situated at a lower elevation than the remainder of the Property.

**[3. Environmental Records Review Summary]{.underline}**

**3.1 Federal Database Review**

The subject property was not identified on the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (\"EPA\") National Priorities List (\"NPL\"), the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Information System (\"CERCLIS\") / Superfund Enterprise Management System (\"SEMS\"), the RCRA Corrective Action (\"CORRACTS\") database, or the RCRA Treatment, Storage, and Disposal (\"TSD\") facility database. The subject property was likewise not identified as a RCRA Small Quantity Generator (\"SQG\") or Large Quantity Generator (\"LQG\").

One adjacent property was identified on federal environmental databases. The property located at **1881 Crescent Boulevard, Maplewood, NJ 07040**, immediately west of and contiguous with the subject property, is listed on the RCRA SQG database in connection with historical dry cleaning operations conducted under the trade name \"Crescent Cleaners,\" which operated at that location from approximately 1978 through 2009. The 1881 Crescent Boulevard facility was identified as a generator of tetrachloroethylene (\"PCE\") waste, classified under EPA Hazardous Waste Codes D039 and F002.

**3.2 State Database Review (NJDEP)**

The subject property is not listed on the New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection (\"NJDEP\") Known Contaminated Sites (\"KCS\") list or the NJDEP Site Remediation Program (\"SRP\") active case list.

The adjacent property at **1881 Crescent Boulevard** is listed on the NJDEP Known Contaminated Sites list, assigned NJDEP SRP Program Interest Number 007624, with a case status of \"Pending.\" NJDEP records indicate that a preliminary assessment was conducted in 2011, which identified PCE contamination in soil and groundwater at concentrations exceeding the NJDEP Soil Remediation Standards established under N.J.A.C. 7:26D and the NJDEP Groundwater Quality Standards established under N.J.A.C. 7:9C. According to the regulatory file, the documented direction of groundwater flow at the 1881 Crescent Boulevard site is generally east-northeast --- that is, from the contamination source toward the subject property.

No underground storage tanks (\"USTs\") were identified as registered at the subject property in the NJDEP UST database.

**3.3 Local Records**

Borough of Maplewood Building Department records confirm the issuance of construction permits for the 2013--2014 development of the subject property. No environmental violations are on file with the Building Department for the subject property. The Borough of Maplewood Health Department similarly had no records of complaints, investigations, or violations related to the subject property.

**3.4 Historical Use Review**

Sanborn fire insurance maps (1925, 1950, and 1970 editions) depict the subject property as vacant or agricultural land. No evidence of prior industrial or commercial use on the subject property itself was identified for any period prior to the 2013--2014 development. Aerial photographs from the 1940 through 2020 series confirm the agricultural and vacant character of the Property prior to commencement of construction in 2013.

The adjacent property at 1881 Crescent Boulevard is first depicted as a commercial laundry and dry cleaning facility on the 1970 Sanborn map, and aerial photographs and city directories confirm continued dry cleaning operations at that address through approximately 2009.

**[4. Site Reconnaissance Observations]{.underline}**

A site reconnaissance of the subject property was conducted on February 27, 2025, by Dr. Anita Rourke, PG, LSRP, Principal, and field technician Michael Voss, both of Greystone Environmental Consulting LLC. Weather conditions at the time of inspection were clear, with an ambient temperature of approximately 38°F and dry ground conditions.

**Building A:** Retail tenants occupying ground-floor spaces at the time of the reconnaissance included a fitness studio, a coffee shop, and an insurance office. Professional office tenants occupied the second and third floors. No evidence of hazardous materials storage, chemical staining, or other environmental distress was observed within or adjacent to Building A. Mechanical systems, including heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (\"HVAC\") equipment, appeared to be in good operating condition. A pad-mounted electrical transformer was observed on the east side of Building A and appeared to be of modern, post-1980 manufacture; no PCB-containing equipment was suspected.

**Building B:** The warehouse and flex space was occupied at the time of the reconnaissance by a distribution and logistics tenant. No drums, containers, or evidence of chemical storage were observed during the interior visual inspection. No floor drains connected to the sanitary sewer system were observed within the warehouse space. A loading dock was observed on the west side of Building B. No evidence of outdoor storage of materials was observed at the time of inspection.

**Parking Areas and Grounds:** The asphalt surface parking lot was observed to be in fair to good condition. No significant staining or evidence of petroleum releases was noted on paved surfaces. Storm drain inlets appeared to connect to the municipal storm sewer system. No evidence of underground storage tanks was observed, including no fill ports, vent pipes, or dispenser pads.

**Eastern Property Boundary:** A vegetated buffer strip was observed along the eastern boundary of the Property, approximately 12 feet in width, consisting primarily of deciduous shrubs and mixed ground cover. The landscape condition is referenced here for observational completeness; evaluation of compliance with zoning buffer requirements is outside the scope of this Phase I ESA.

**Northeastern Corner of Property:** This area, comprising approximately 0.3 acres (13,068 square feet), was observed to be at a lower grade than the remainder of the site. Evidence of periodic inundation was noted during the reconnaissance, including hydric soil indicators (dark, mottled soil observed in exposed areas near the pavement edge), wetland-type vegetation along the northern edge of the property, and sediment deposits on paved surfaces near the rear curb cut on Elm Terrace. This area corresponds to the **FEMA Flood Zone AE designation** (100-year floodplain) as identified on Federal Emergency Management Agency (\"FEMA\") Flood Insurance Rate Map (\"FIRM\") Panel No. 34013C0038J, with an effective date of June 4, 2021. The **Base Flood Elevation (\"BFE\") for this area is 42 feet NAVD88.** Per the ALTA/NSPS Land Title Survey prepared by Cartwright Surveying Associates (dated February 28, 2025), the ground floor elevation of Building A is **44.5 feet NAVD88**, which is approximately 2.5 feet above the established BFE.

**Adjacent Property --- 1881 Crescent Boulevard:** The adjacent property to the west was observed from the subject property boundary. The former dry cleaning facility at 1881 Crescent Boulevard appears to consist of a vacant single-story commercial building. No active operations were observed at the time of the reconnaissance. A chain-link fence separates the two properties along the shared boundary. No monitoring wells were observed on the subject property during the reconnaissance. However, two monitoring well covers were observed on the 1881 Crescent Boulevard side of the property line, within approximately 15 to 20 feet of the shared boundary, suggesting active or recent groundwater monitoring activity associated with the known contamination at that site.

**[5. Findings and Opinions]{.underline}**

**5.1 Recognized Environmental Conditions (RECs)**

**REC-1: Potential Tetrachloroethylene (PCE) Migration from 1881 Crescent Boulevard**

Historical dry cleaning operations at the adjacent property to the west (1881 Crescent Boulevard, Maplewood, NJ 07040) were conducted from approximately 1978 through 2009. Tetrachloroethylene (\"PCE\"), a chlorinated volatile organic compound (\"CVOC\") commonly used as a dry cleaning solvent, has been documented in soil and groundwater at the 1881 Crescent Boulevard property at concentrations exceeding applicable NJDEP Soil Remediation Standards (N.J.A.C. 7:26D) and Groundwater Quality Standards (N.J.A.C. 7:9C).

The documented direction of groundwater flow at the 1881 Crescent Boulevard site is east-northeast --- that is, from the contamination source toward the subject property. The NJDEP Site Remediation Program case (PI No. 007624) remains in \"Pending\" status, indicating that no final remediation has been completed or approved by the NJDEP. Additionally, two monitoring wells were observed within 15 to 20 feet of the shared property boundary during the site reconnaissance, suggesting that the contamination plume may extend to or near the property line separating 1881 Crescent Boulevard from the subject property.

**Opinion:** Based on the proximity of the documented contamination source, the direction of groundwater flow toward the subject property, the well-documented persistence and mobility of PCE in subsurface environments (including its tendency to migrate as a dense non-aqueous phase liquid and to generate vapor-phase contamination), and the pending status of the remediation case at 1881 Crescent Boulevard, Greystone identifies a **Recognized Environmental Condition (REC)** in connection with the subject property. In the professional judgment of the undersigned environmental professionals, there is a reasonable possibility that PCE contamination has migrated onto the subject property in soil vapor and/or groundwater.

**Note Regarding New Jersey Regulatory Implications:** The User and User\'s counsel should be aware that a transfer of ownership of commercial or industrial property in New Jersey may trigger notification and remediation obligations under the New Jersey Industrial Site Recovery Act (\"ISRA\"), N.J.S.A. 13:1K-6 et seq., and/or the Site Remediation Reform Act (\"SRRA\"), N.J.S.A. 58:10C-1 et seq. If contamination attributable to the 1881 Crescent Boulevard source or any other source is confirmed on the subject property, the Property could become subject to a remediation obligation that must be addressed through the NJDEP\'s Licensed Site Remediation Professional (\"LSRP\") program. Greystone recommends that the User\'s environmental and legal counsel evaluate potential ISRA and SRRA triggering events in connection with this transaction prior to closing.

**5.2 Controlled Recognized Environmental Conditions (CRECs)**

No Controlled Recognized Environmental Conditions were identified in connection with the subject property.

**5.3 Historical Recognized Environmental Conditions (HRECs)**

No Historical Recognized Environmental Conditions were identified in connection with the subject property.

**5.4 Other Environmental Considerations (Not RECs)**

The following conditions do not constitute Recognized Environmental Conditions under ASTM E1527-21 but are disclosed as environmental considerations relevant to the User\'s evaluation of the subject property:

**FEMA Flood Zone AE Designation:** Approximately 0.3 acres (13,068 square feet) of the northeastern corner of the subject property is located within FEMA Flood Zone AE (100-year floodplain) as delineated on FIRM Panel No. 34013C0038J (effective date June 4, 2021). The Base Flood Elevation for this area is 42 feet NAVD88. The nearest existing structure, Building A, has a ground floor elevation of 44.5 feet NAVD88, which is approximately 2.5 feet above the BFE. While the flood zone designation is not a Recognized Environmental Condition under ASTM E1527-21, **this condition is disclosed as an environmental consideration that may affect future development, expansion, or regrading activities in the northeastern portion of the Property.** Any such activities within the designated flood zone would be subject to FEMA floodplain development requirements, including potential requirements for flood-proofing, elevation certificates, and compliance with the Borough of Maplewood\'s Flood Damage Prevention Ordinance and the NJDEP Flood Hazard Area Control Act regulations (N.J.A.C. 7:13). The User should consider this constraint in evaluating the redevelopment potential of the Property.

**Radon:** Essex County, New Jersey is classified as EPA Radon Zone 2 (moderate potential for elevated indoor radon levels). No radon testing was performed as part of this Phase I ESA, as radon testing is outside the standard scope of ASTM E1527-21. If enclosed below-grade or ground-level occupied spaces are planned as part of any future development or renovation, Greystone recommends that radon testing be performed.

**Wetlands:** Minor hydric soil indicators were observed in the northeastern corner of the subject property during the site reconnaissance. No formal wetland delineation was conducted as part of this assessment. If development or site disturbance is contemplated in this area, a freshwater wetland delineation by a qualified professional is recommended to determine whether areas subject to the Freshwater Wetlands Protection Act (N.J.S.A. 13:9B-1 et seq.) are present.

**[6. Recommendations]{.underline}**

Based on the findings of this Phase I ESA, Greystone makes the following recommendations:

**Phase II Environmental Site Assessment:** Greystone strongly recommends that a Phase II Environmental Site Assessment be conducted to evaluate whether PCE contamination from 1881 Crescent Boulevard has migrated onto the subject property. The recommended Phase II scope of work should include the following:

> • Installation of at least three soil borings along the western property boundary and within the interior of the site to assess subsurface soil and soil vapor conditions;
>
> • Collection and laboratory analysis of soil samples for chlorinated volatile organic compounds (\"CVOCs\") using EPA Method 8260;
>
> • Installation of at least two temporary or permanent groundwater monitoring wells to assess groundwater quality for CVOCs;
>
> • Sub-slab soil vapor sampling beneath Building A and Building B if initial analytical results indicate vapor intrusion potential; and
>
> • Comparison of all analytical results to applicable NJDEP Soil Remediation Standards (N.J.A.C. 7:26D), Groundwater Quality Standards (N.J.A.C. 7:9C), and Vapor Intrusion Screening Levels.

**Estimated Phase II Timeline:** Greystone estimates a period of four to six weeks from authorization to receipt of laboratory analytical results and delivery of the final Phase II ESA report. Given the **inspection contingency expiration date of July 18, 2025**, as identified in the User questionnaire, the User should authorize Phase II work promptly if it intends to complete the subsurface investigation within the contingency period. As of the date of this report (March 15, 2025), approximately four months remain before the contingency deadline, which provides adequate time for a Phase II investigation if authorization is obtained in a timely manner.

**ISRA/SRRA Evaluation:** Greystone recommends that the User\'s legal counsel (Holloway Stern LLP) evaluate whether the proposed transaction triggers ISRA applicability based on the North American Industry Classification System (\"NAICS\") codes applicable to current or former operations at the subject property and at the adjacent property, and whether any SRRA obligations would attach to the subject property upon transfer of ownership. If PCE contamination is confirmed on the subject property through Phase II investigation, the User should assess the estimated cost and timeline of remediation through the NJDEP LSRP program prior to closing, and should consider appropriate contractual protections in the purchase and sale agreement.

**Flood Zone Considerations:** The User should consult with its land use counsel and design professionals regarding any planned improvements, expansions, or regrading activities in the northeastern portion of the Property to ensure compliance with applicable FEMA floodplain development regulations, the Borough of Maplewood Flood Damage Prevention Ordinance, and the NJDEP Flood Hazard Area Control Act regulations. Greystone recommends obtaining an Elevation Certificate for any structures proposed within or near the Flood Zone AE boundary.

**[7. Limitations, Qualifications, and Disclaimers]{.underline}**

This Phase I Environmental Site Assessment was performed in conformance with the scope and limitations of ASTM E1527-21, \"Standard Practice for Environmental Site Assessments: Phase I Environmental Site Assessment Process.\" The assessment has inherent limitations based on the defined scope of the investigation, including the following:

No sampling of soil, groundwater, soil vapor, surface water, sediment, building materials, or air was conducted as part of this Phase I ESA. The identification of Recognized Environmental Conditions is based solely on non-invasive investigation, including records review, historical research, site reconnaissance, and interviews.

This report is based on information reasonably available at the time of the investigation. Conditions may exist at the subject property that were not identified during this assessment due to limitations in available records, access restrictions imposed by property owners or tenants, or subsurface conditions that are not observable through surface reconnaissance methods.

The findings and conclusions presented in this report are professional opinions based on the data gathered during the course of the assessment and are subject to the limitations inherent in that data. Environmental conditions are subject to change over time, and the conclusions of this report may not remain valid indefinitely.

This report does not constitute a legal opinion on compliance with environmental laws or regulations. The User is advised to consult with qualified legal counsel regarding the regulatory implications of the findings presented herein, including but not limited to obligations under ISRA, SRRA, CERCLA, and applicable state and federal environmental statutes.

This report has been prepared for the exclusive use of Crescent Boulevard Holdings LLC (and its parent entity, Redfield Capital Partners LLC) and their legal counsel, Holloway Stern LLP, and the User\'s lender, Briarcliff National Bank, solely in connection with the proposed acquisition of the subject property. No other party may rely on this report without the prior written consent of Greystone Environmental Consulting LLC.

The shelf life of this Phase I ESA is 180 days from the date of the report, that is, through **September 11, 2025**, in accordance with ASTM E1527-21, Section 4.6. If the transaction has not closed by that date, the Phase I ESA may need to be updated or a new assessment conducted to maintain the validity of the All Appropriate Inquiries standard.

This report does not address business environmental risk, mold, lead-based paint, asbestos-containing materials, radon (beyond the general notation in Section 5.4), or other environmental conditions outside the defined scope of ASTM E1527-21, unless specifically noted herein.

Greystone Environmental Consulting LLC has performed this Phase I Environmental Site Assessment with the degree of care and skill ordinarily exercised under similar circumstances by reputable environmental professionals practicing in the State of New Jersey at the time this assessment was conducted. No other warranty, express or implied, is made.

**[8. Signatures and Certification]{.underline}**

I hereby certify that this Phase I Environmental Site Assessment was conducted in accordance with ASTM E1527-21, \"Standard Practice for Environmental Site Assessments: Phase I Environmental Site Assessment Process,\" and that the findings and opinions expressed herein represent my professional judgment based on the information obtained during this assessment.

def add_rich(par, text, size=None, color=None, bold_all=False, italic_all=False):
    """Parse **bold** and _italic_ inline markers."""
    tokens = re.split(r"(\*\*.+?\*\*|__.+?__)", text)
    for tk in tokens:
        if not tk: continue
        if tk.startswith("**") and tk.endswith("**") and len(tk) > 4:
            r = par.add_run(tk[2:-2]); r.bold = True
        elif tk.startswith("__") and tk.endswith("__") and len(tk) > 4:

        else:

        if bold_all: r.bold = True
