tool_calls.arguments:
{"command": "cd "$WORKSPACE_DIR"; cat > build/p5_critical.py <<'PYEOF'
# ================= 4. CRITICAL ISSUES =================
doc.add_page_break()
H1("Critical Issues", "4")
P("Each of the six issues below defeats the Report's conclusion in whole or in part. Each requires a variance, an approval, or a cure that is not presently in hand. Because the Inspection Period closes on **July 18, 2025** and Closing is set for **August 15, 2025**, each must be resolved, or expressly priced and allocated, before the earlier date. We note at the outset that the Report's Section I contains the unqualified statement that \"**No other variances, waivers, or exceptions are required for the existing improvements and uses on the property as currently configured.**\" That statement is incorrect in respect of at least C-1, C-2, C-3 and C-6.")

# ---- C-1 ----
H2("4.1  C-1 — Rear yard setback: a 7-foot deficiency on the north boundary, certified as compliant")
label_par("What the Report says.", "Section IV.A lists the B-3 minimum rear yard setback as \"25 feet\" with no qualification, and states that \"The minimum rear yard setback in the B-3 district is 25 feet per § 245-18.\" Section IV.B records \"Rear Yard — North (abutting R-4) | 25 ft minimum | 28 ft (Building A) | **COMPLIANT**.\" Section IV.C concludes that \"The 28-foot rear yard setback exceeds the 25-foot minimum rear yard setback required by § 245-18. This standard is met.\" Section IX.A repeats \"Rear Yard Setback — North (abutting R-4) | COMPLIANT.\"")
label_par("What the record shows.", "Ordinance § 245-18(h)(3) provides that \"The minimum rear yard setback shall be twenty-five (25) feet. **Where a rear yard abuts a residential zone (R-1, R-2, R-3, R-4, or R-5), the minimum rear yard setback shall be increased to thirty-five (35) feet.**\" The summary table at § 245-18(j) states the standard as \"Rear Yard Setback — 25 feet (35 feet abutting residential zone).\" The Survey expressly records the applicable requirement as \"**35 ft min. (residential buffer)**\" and the measured setback as **28.0 ft**, and in Note 2 records that the north boundary abuts Lots 5 and 6, Block 413, which are \"classified R-4 Residential,\" that the measured setback \"is 7.0 feet less than the residential buffer requirement,\" and that \"No variance or other land use approval for this setback reduction was provided to the surveyor.\"")
label_par("Analysis.", "The Report had the predicate for the enhanced standard and applied it on one boundary but not the other. Its own Section 3.3 states that the property abuts R-4 on the north and east and that \"certain bulk standards in the B-3 district are enhanced when a property abuts a residential zone.\" In Section IV.A the Report reproduces the side yard enhancement faithfully — \"15 feet (25 feet when abutting a residential zone)\" — while silently dropping the identical parenthetical from the rear yard line. This is not a difference of planning judgment; it is a selective transcription of a parenthetical that appears, in the same form, in both rows of the ordinance table. The consequence is a **7.0-foot shortfall (28.0 ft against 35.0 ft)** that the Report certifies as compliance.")
P("The Report also fails to engage the mechanism by which such a shortfall might be lawfully excused. It does not mention § 245-55 at all. If the enhanced 35-foot rear yard standard was **not** in effect when Building A was constructed in 2014, the building may enjoy protection as a lawfully pre-existing nonconforming structure under § 245-55(a) and N.J.S.A. 40:55D-68 — but the burden of establishing that status rests on the owner under § 245-55(a), and § 245-55(d) would then bar any enlargement, extension, reconstruction or structural alteration of Building A that does not conform. If the standard **was** in effect in 2014, the building was constructed in violation of it and requires a variance. On either branch of the analysis the Report's \"COMPLIANT\" is wrong, and the Report never undertakes the inquiry that would distinguish the two. We raise the dating of the standard as an open question at Section 10 (OQ-1).")
label_par("A compounding problem.", "Section 245-18(h)(3) is not only a dimensional standard. It further provides that \"**No portion of any building, structure, parking area, loading area, or dumpster enclosure shall be located within the enhanced rear yard setback when the rear yard abuts a residential zone**, except for landscaping and stormwater management facilities expressly approved by the Planning Board.\" This clause is an outright prohibition rather than a setback to be measured, and nonconforming-structure protection under § 245-55 does not reach it. The Survey and the ESA both place the Building B loading dock and apron, and part of the rear parking area, in the northern portion of the site directly abutting the R-4 boundary. That is developed at H-2 and M-8.")
label_par("Consequence.", "The property does not comply with § 245-18(h)(3) and holds no relief from it. A bulk variance, or (if the standard post-dates 2014) a documented nonconforming-structure determination, is required. Because the enhanced setback also prohibits the parking and loading uses now conducted in the north yard, a variance limited to the building line would not by itself cure the site.")
label_par("Required action.", "Obtain (i) the zoning history confirming the effective date of the 35-foot enhanced rear setback; (ii) a corrected setback analysis; and (iii) either a variance application or a § 245-55 nonconforming determination, in each case addressing the building, the loading area and the rear parking together.")

# ---- C-2 ----
H2("4.2  C-2 — Warehouse/flex use occupies 30.58% of gross floor area against a 25% ceiling")
label_par("What the Report says.", "Section V.C(d) states that \"The warehouse/flex use represents approximately **24%** of the total gross floor area on the site, which is within the 25% maximum prescribed by § 245-15(c)(3)(d). This condition is satisfied.\" Section V.C closes: \"the warehouse/flex conditional use in Building B is in compliance with all applicable conditions of § 245-15(c)(3).\"")
label_par("What the record shows.", "Section 245-15(c)(3)(d) provides that \"The gross floor area devoted to warehouse, distribution, or flex space use **shall not exceed twenty-five percent (25%)** of the total gross floor area of all structures on the lot,\" with gross floor area as defined in § 245-18(g). The inputs are not in dispute: Building B is 18,500 SF and total GFA on the lot is 60,500 SF (42,000 + 18,500), a figure the Report states correctly in the same paragraph and which is confirmed by the Survey at Section 5.")
label_par("Analysis.", "The quotient is **18,500 ÷ 60,500 = 30.58%**, not 24%. Applying the ceiling of 25% to total GFA of 60,500 SF gives a permitted warehouse/flex floor area of **15,125 SF**; the existing 18,500 SF exceeds it by **3,375 SF**. No computation on the correct 60,500 SF base can produce 24%; a result near 24% requires a denominator of approximately 77,000 SF, which has no support anywhere in the record. This is the clearest arithmetic failure in the Report, and it is outcome-determinative: it converts a conclusion of comfortable compliance into a **5.58 percentage-point violation** of a condition the Board must find satisfied before it can approve the use.")
label_par("Consequence.", "The warehouse/flex use cannot be approved as configured. The shortfall can be cured in one of three ways, each with different consequences: reduce the warehouse/flex floor area in Building B to 15,125 SF or less; reallocate floor area so that total GFA rises without increasing warehouse/flex area (for example by adding a permitted use elsewhere, which would also need to satisfy the FAR, coverage and parking standards); or obtain relief from the conditional use standard, which requires a variance and is in any event discretionary. Standing alone this issue would prevent a conditional use approval; combined with C-3 it means the use has no approval at all.")
label_par("Required action.", "Recompute the ratio and require the Seller to identify the basis for the 24% figure. Any cure should be modelled against the parking requirement, because reducing warehouse area changes the § 245-42(b) parking calculation.")

# ---- C-3 ----
H2("4.3  C-3 — No Planning Board conditional use approval for the warehouse/flex use")
label_par("What the Report says.", "Section V.C concludes: \"No conditional use approval from the Planning Board **appears to be required** beyond the conditions satisfied by the site as currently configured.\" The Report's Section V.B nevertheless classifies the warehouse/flex use correctly as a \"Conditional Use\" under § 245-15(c)(3).")
label_par("What the record shows.", "Section 245-15(c) provides that conditional uses are permitted \"subject to **approval by the Planning Board** upon a finding that the conditions specified herein and the general conditional use standards of § 245-22 are satisfied,\" and that \"The Planning Board may impose reasonable conditions upon any conditional use approval.\" The variance resolution addresses the point twice and without ambiguity. Paragraph 2(5) finds that the warehouse/flex use \"is classified as a conditional use ... and that the Applicant has indicated its intention to seek, or will be required to obtain, **separate conditional use approval** from the Maplewood Planning Board in connection with that use,\" and states that the variance relief \"**does not constitute, and shall not be construed as, conditional use approval**, site plan approval, or any other form of land use approval other than the specific bulk variance described herein.\" Condition 5 independently obliges the Applicant to obtain \"conditional use approval for the warehouse/flex use from the Maplewood Planning Board.\" The Report itself lists the resolution among the documents reviewed and summarises it at Section VI and Appendix B — but omits paragraph 2(5) and Condition 5 entirely.")
label_par("Analysis.", "There are only three possibilities, and the Report reconciles none of them. Either a conditional use approval exists and was not produced, or it does not exist and the use has been operating since 2014 without the approval the ordinance requires, or the Report's view that no approval is needed is correct — which would contradict both § 245-15(c) and the Board's express findings. The first is a document request; the second is the most likely and is a live zoning violation; the third is not tenable. The Report's closing sentence — that no conditional use approval \"appears to be required\" — is an assertion of legal conclusion that the Report elsewhere disclaims the competence to make (Section 2.3(2) states that the Report \"does not constitute a legal opinion\").")
label_par("Consequence.", "The warehouse/flex use is a conditional use operating without conditional use approval. It is therefore neither a permitted use nor an approved conditional use, and § 245-15(d)(7) provides that any use not expressly listed as a permitted principal use, permitted accessory use or conditional use \"shall be deemed prohibited.\" The use is exposed to enforcement under § 245-62, including per-diem penalties, and no certificate of compliance could properly have issued for Building B under § 245-60(b), which forbids issuance until \"all conditions of approval have been satisfied.\" A Planning Board application is required, and it cannot succeed as configured because of C-2 and H-2.")
label_par("Required action.", "Request from the Seller the complete conditional use file, including any Planning Board resolution and the site plan approval said to underlie the 2014 construction. Absent production, treat the use as unapproved and make conditional use approval a Closing condition.")

# ---- C-4 ----
H2("4.4  C-4 — The variance is personal to the Seller and expires on transfer")
label_par("What the Report says.", "Section VI states that \"The Board's resolution memorializes these conditions as binding obligations running with the variance approval. **The variance remains in effect and the property benefits from this approval.**\" Section I and Section IX.A each rely on the variance as the sole qualification to an otherwise unqualified finding of compliance. Appendix B summarises the resolution as granting \"a reduced east side yard setback of 18 feet\" and says nothing further. The Report nowhere mentions transferability, and it does not mention the 90-day confirmation mechanism at all.")
label_par("What the record shows.", "Section 4 of the resolution provides that the variance \"is **personal to the Applicant**, Maplewood Gateway Associates LP, and its principals,\" and that it \"shall expire automatically upon the occurrence of\" either \"(a) the approved use is discontinued for a period of twelve (12) consecutive months\" or \"(b) **the property is transferred, conveyed, assigned, or otherwise alienated** to any person or entity other than the Applicant ... **UNLESS the successor owner, transferee, or assignee files an application with this Board for confirmation of the variance within ninety (90) days of the date of transfer**.\" It continues: \"Failure to file such application within the ninety (90) day period shall result in the **automatic expiration** of this variance, and the property shall thereafter be required to comply with the full setback requirements of § 245-18.\" The Board also \"reserves the right, upon any such confirmation application, to impose additional or modified conditions.\" The Survey flags the point twice — in the surveyor's note at Section 1 and again at Section 10.1(8) — and expressly declines to opine on it.")
label_par("Analysis.", "The sale to Crescent Boulevard Holdings LLC is a transfer within limb (b). On Closing the variance expires by its own terms unless the Buyer files a confirmation application within 90 days, and even then the Board may impose additional or modified conditions. Two points follow. First, the Report's phrase \"binding obligations running with the variance approval\" glosses the distinction that matters: under § 245-58(b) the **conditions** bind successors and assigns, but under § 4 of the resolution the **variance itself** does not run with the land. Second, without the variance the east side yard setback of 19.0 ft (Survey, Section 4) stands against the enhanced 25-foot requirement of § 245-18(h)(2) — a **6.0-foot deficiency** with no relief of any kind.")
P("The practical consequence is larger than the setback itself. Without the variance, Building B becomes at best a nonconforming structure under § 245-55(d), which may be \"maintained and repaired but shall not be enlarged, extended, reconstructed, or structurally altered\" unless the work conforms to current requirements. That would sterilise the very expansion the Report promotes. Section IX.B(2) of the Report tells the Buyer that the FAR of 0.3307 against a 1.50 maximum indicates \"significant remaining development capacity\" and that \"Any future expansion or development would have considerable room within the existing FAR limitations.\" That advice is materially incomplete: the binding constraint on expansion is not FAR but the east side yard, and the relief that makes the east side yard tolerable lapses on Closing.")
label_par("Consequence.", "The property's only dimensional relief is time-limited and conditional on action by the Buyer after Closing. If the confirmation application is not filed by roughly **November 13, 2025** (90 days from an August 15, 2025 Closing), the variance expires automatically and cannot be revived by the Buyer without a fresh application. Both the east setback and Building B's development potential are at stake.")
label_par("Required action.", "Make the variance's survival a Closing condition. The Seller should either procure a fresh variance that runs with the land, or join with the Buyer in a confirmation application to the Board under § 4, with the Buyer participating so as to be heard on any additional conditions. The Buyer should also calendar the 90-day deadline on the day of Closing, and consider whether the PSA's 24-month survival period for the § 5.3 zoning representations (PSA § 5.7) is long enough to reach a lapsed variance.")

# ---- C-5 ----
H2("4.5  C-5 — The east landscape buffer fails on width and on species")
label_par("What the Report says.", "Section IV.B records \"Landscaped Buffer — East | Required per variance condition | Landscape buffer exists along the eastern boundary | **COMPLIANT**.\" Section IV.C states that \"A landscape buffer is maintained along the eastern property boundary **in accordance with this condition**.\" Section VI, addressing compliance with Condition 1, states that \"a landscape buffer is maintained along the eastern property boundary in accordance with this condition.\" Section IX.A records \"Landscape Buffer — East | COMPLIANT.\"")
label_par("What the record shows.", "Condition 1 of the resolution requires a \"**fifteen (15) foot wide evergreen landscape buffer** along the entire eastern property boundary,\" consisting of \"a minimum of one (1) evergreen tree per eight (8) linear feet of boundary, with a minimum planting height of six (6) feet at the time of installation, supplemented by evergreen shrubs planted in staggered rows to create a continuous visual screen achieving a minimum opacity of seventy-five percent (75%) within two (2) growing seasons,\" on a landscape plan prepared by a licensed landscape architect and \"submitted to the Borough Zoning Officer for review and approval prior to the issuance of a Certificate of Occupancy for Building B.\" Section 245-18(i) independently requires a 15-foot buffer planted with a mix of evergreen trees and shrubs sufficient to provide year-round screening to a minimum height of six feet within three years.")
P("The Survey, at Section 7, measured the buffer at three cross-sections: **11.8 ft** at the north end, **12.2 ft** at the midpoint and **12.0 ft** at the south end, for an **average of 12.0 ft**. It records that the plantings are \"sparse deciduous trees and shrubs, predominantly maple (__Acer__ spp.) and ornamental cherry (__Prunus__ spp.),\" that \"**No evergreen species were identified** along the buffer at the time of the field survey,\" that there was \"No continuous ground cover planting,\" and that \"No fencing was observed.\" The surveyor notes that the measured width is \"3.0 feet less than the required 15.0 feet\" and that the plantings are \"predominantly deciduous rather than evergreen.\" The ESA, at Section 4, independently recorded a buffer \"approximately 12 feet in width, consisting primarily of deciduous shrubs.\" (It did so expressly without addressing zoning compliance, as it was entitled to do.)")
label_par("Analysis.", "Three of the four elements of Condition 1 fail on the face of the field evidence: **width** (12.0 ft against 15.0 ft, a 20% shortfall sustained across all three cross-sections and not attributable to a single narrow point); **composition** (no evergreen species at all, where evergreens are the specified and only acceptable means of achieving year-round screening); and **continuous screen** (sparse plantings, no continuous ground cover, opacity untested but plainly not 75%). A fourth element — whether the licensed landscape architect's plan was approved by the Zoning Officer before the Building B certificate of occupancy issued — cannot be tested on the record before us and is carried as a document request.")
P("The Report's method is the source of the error. It did not measure the buffer; it did not commission a measurement; and it conducted no site visit (Section 2.3(5) of the Report confirms this). It asserted compliance from the existence of vegetation. The Survey, which the Report relies on for every other dimension in the document, contains the contradictory measurement in a section the Report does not cite.")
label_par("Consequence.", "This is a breach of a condition of variance approval, and § 245-62(a) provides that a violation of \"any condition of a variance approval\" is subject to the penalties established by N.J.S.A. 40:55D-18, with each day after a notice to cure constituting a separate offence. More importantly for the transaction, the buffer is the consideration on which the Board's findings rest. Finding 2 of the resolution grants relief \"provided that adequate buffering and screening is installed along the entire eastern boundary\" and finds that \"the conditions imposed herein will adequately protect\" the neighbouring residents. A deficient buffer therefore does two things at once: it is an enforceable violation, and it supplies the Board with a ready basis to impose additional or modified conditions on the § 4 confirmation application — a live risk given C-4.")
label_par("Required action.", "Either restore the buffer to Condition 1 (15.0 ft clear width, one evergreen per 8 linear feet at 6 ft minimum installation height, staggered evergreen shrubs to 75% opacity) with Zoning Officer sign-off, or obtain a modification of Condition 1 from the Board. Restoration should be costed as part of the cure package, since the eastern boundary also carries the 19-foot building setback that limits any re-grading.")

# ---- C-6 ----
H2("4.6  C-6 — Monument sign exceeds the B-3 height and area limits; the Report applied the wrong district's standards")
label_par("What the Report says.", "Section VIII.A correctly states the B-3 standard: monument signs are subject to \"maximum sign height of 6 feet above finished grade; maximum sign face area of 32 square feet.\" Section VIII.B then records the existing monument sign as \"8 ft height, 48 SF face\" and certifies it \"**COMPLIANT**.\" Section VIII.C states that \"The monument sign is consistent with the character of the B-3 district\" and that the sign \"was permitted under the building permit records reviewed.\" Section IX.A records \"Signage | COMPLIANT.\"")
label_par("What the record shows.", "Section 245-50(c)(1)(ii) limits monument sign height to \"**six (6) feet** measured from the finished grade at the base of the sign to the highest point of the sign structure,\" inclusive of \"the base and all structural and decorative elements.\" Subsection (iii) limits sign face area to \"**thirty-two (32) square feet per side**.\" The Survey, at Section 3.1, records the monument sign as having \"a measured height of 8 feet and a sign face area of approximately 48 square feet (double-faced).\"")
label_par("Analysis.", "The sign exceeds both limits: **2 feet over on height (33% over)** and **16 square feet over on area per side (50% over)**. The explanation is visible on the face of the Report. Eight feet and 48 square feet are precisely the monument sign standards for the adjoining **B-2 General Business District**, set out at § 245-50(d)(1). The Report has taken its statement of the governing standard from the B-3 subsection and its determination of compliance from the B-2 subsection, and the contradiction sits within a single two-page section. That is not a matter of interpretation; § 245-50(c) is expressly confined to the B-3 district.")
P("Nor is the sign saved by the nonconforming-sign provisions. Section 245-50(i) protects a sign \"lawfully erected prior to the adoption or amendment of this section,\" but a nonconforming sign \"may continue to be maintained but shall not be enlarged, relocated, or structurally altered,\" and must be removed if abandoned or if the associated use is discontinued for 90 days. Even on the most favourable view — that the sign was lawfully permitted in 2014 under a standard then permitting eight feet — it is a nonconforming sign, not a compliant one, and the Report's certification is wrong in either case. We flag the 2014 permit position as an open question at Section 10 (OQ-2).")
label_par("Consequence.", "The sign requires physical reduction, replacement, or a variance, and a sign permit under § 245-50 (which requires a Construction Official's sign permit for all signs not exempt under § 245-50(h) — the Report instead cites \"building permit records,\" which is a different instrument). The exposure is modest in cost but the issue matters because it is one of three items the Report certifies as compliant on the basis on an incorrect statement of the governing standard, which goes to the weight of the Report as a whole.")
label_par("Required action.", "Require the Seller to produce the sign permit history and either reduce the sign to 6 ft and 32 SF per side or obtain a variance; and require a corrected sign compliance statement covering the additional matters at M-5.")

{"command": "cd "$WORKSPACE_DIR"; cat > build/p5_critical.py <<'PYEOF'
# ================= 4. CRITICAL ISSUES =================
doc.add_page_break()
H1("Critical Issues", "4")
P("Each of the six issues below defeats the Report's conclusion in whole or in part. Each requires a variance, an approval, or a cure that is not presently in hand. Because the Inspection Period closes on **July 18, 2025** and Closing is set for **August 15, 2025**, each must be resolved, or expressly priced and allocated, before the earlier date. We note at the outset that the Report's Section I contains the unqualified statement that \"**No other variances, waivers, or exceptions are required for the existing improvements and uses on the property as currently configured.**\" That statement is incorrect in respect of at least C-1, C-2, C-3 and C-6.")

# ---- C-1 ----
H2("4.1  C-1 — Rear yard setback: a 7-foot deficiency on the north boundary, certified as compliant")
label_par("What the Report says.", "Section IV.A lists the B-3 minimum rear yard setback as \"25 feet\" with no qualification, and states that \"The minimum rear yard setback in the B-3 district is 25 feet per § 245-18.\" Section IV.B records \"Rear Yard — North (abutting R-4) | 25 ft minimum | 28 ft (Building A) | **COMPLIANT**.\" Section IV.C concludes that \"The 28-foot rear yard setback exceeds the 25-foot minimum rear yard setback required by § 245-18. This standard is met.\" Section IX.A repeats \"Rear Yard Setback — North (abutting R-4) | COMPLIANT.\"")
label_par("What the record shows.", "Ordinance § 245-18(h)(3) provides that \"The minimum rear yard setback shall be twenty-five (25) feet. **Where a rear yard abuts a residential zone (R-1, R-2, R-3, R-4, or R-5), the minimum rear yard setback shall be increased to thirty-five (35) feet.**\" The summary table at § 245-18(j) states the standard as \"Rear Yard Setback — 25 feet (35 feet abutting residential zone).\" The Survey expressly records the applicable requirement as \"**35 ft min. (residential buffer)**\" and the measured setback as **28.0 ft**, and in Note 2 records that the north boundary abuts Lots 5 and 6, Block 413, which are \"classified R-4 Residential,\" that the measured setback \"is 7.0 feet less than the residential buffer requirement,\" and that \"No variance or other land use approval for this setback reduction was provided to the surveyor.\"")
label_par("Analysis.", "The Report had the predicate for the enhanced standard and applied it on one boundary but not the other. Its own Section 3.3 states that the property abuts R-4 on the north and east and that \"certain bulk standards in the B-3 district are enhanced when a property abuts a residential zone.\" In Section IV.A the Report reproduces the side yard enhancement faithfully — \"15 feet (25 feet when abutting a residential zone)\" — while silently dropping the identical parenthetical from the rear yard line. This is not a difference of planning judgment; it is a selective transcription of a parenthetical that appears, in the same form, in both rows of the ordinance table. The consequence is a **7.0-foot shortfall (28.0 ft against 35.0 ft)** that the Report certifies as compliance.")
P("The Report also fails to engage the mechanism by which such a shortfall might be lawfully excused. It does not mention § 245-55 at all. If the enhanced 35-foot rear yard standard was **not** in effect when Building A was constructed in 2014, the building may enjoy protection as a lawfully pre-existing nonconforming structure under § 245-55(a) and N.J.S.A. 40:55D-68 — but the burden of establishing that status rests on the owner under § 245-55(a), and § 245-55(d) would then bar any enlargement, extension, reconstruction or structural alteration of Building A that does not conform. If the standard **was** in effect in 2014, the building was constructed in violation of it and requires a variance. On either branch of the analysis the Report's \"COMPLIANT\" is wrong, and the Report never undertakes the inquiry that would distinguish the two. We raise the dating of the standard as an open question at Section 10 (OQ-1).")
label_par("A compounding problem.", "Section 245-18(h)(3) is not only a dimensional standard. It further provides that \"**No portion of any building, structure, parking area, loading area, or dumpster enclosure shall be located within the enhanced rear yard setback when the rear yard abuts a residential zone**, except for landscaping and stormwater management facilities expressly approved by the Planning Board.\" This clause is an outright prohibition rather than a setback to be measured, and nonconforming-structure protection under § 245-55 does not reach it. The Survey and the ESA both place the Building B loading dock and apron, and part of the rear parking area, in the northern portion of the site directly abutting the R-4 boundary. That is developed at H-2 and M-8.")
label_par("Consequence.", "The property does not comply with § 245-18(h)(3) and holds no relief from it. A bulk variance, or (if the standard post-dates 2014) a documented nonconforming-structure determination, is required. Because the enhanced setback also prohibits the parking and loading uses now conducted in the north yard, a variance limited to the building line would not by itself cure the site.")
label_par("Required action.", "Obtain (i) the zoning history confirming the effective date of the 35-foot enhanced rear setback; (ii) a corrected setback analysis; and (iii) either a variance application or a § 245-55 nonconforming determination, in each case addressing the building, the loading area and the rear parking together.")

# ---- C-2 ----
H2("4.2  C-2 — Warehouse/flex use occupies 30.58% of gross floor area against a 25% ceiling")
label_par("What the Report says.", "Section V.C(d) states that \"The warehouse/flex use represents approximately **24%** of the total gross floor area on the site, which is within the 25% maximum prescribed by § 245-15(c)(3)(d). This condition is satisfied.\" Section V.C closes: \"the warehouse/flex conditional use in Building B is in compliance with all applicable conditions of § 245-15(c)(3).\"")
label_par("What the record shows.", "Section 245-15(c)(3)(d) provides that \"The gross floor area devoted to warehouse, distribution, or flex space use **shall not exceed twenty-five percent (25%)** of the total gross floor area of all structures on the lot,\" with gross floor area as defined in § 245-18(g). The inputs are not in dispute: Building B is 18,500 SF and total GFA on the lot is 60,500 SF (42,000 + 18,500), a figure the Report states correctly in the same paragraph and which is confirmed by the Survey at Section 5.")
label_par("Analysis.", "The quotient is **18,500 ÷ 60,500 = 30.58%**, not 24%. Applying the ceiling of 25% to total GFA of 60,500 SF gives a permitted warehouse/flex floor area of **15,125 SF**; the existing 18,500 SF exceeds it by **3,375 SF**. No computation on the correct 60,500 SF base can produce 24%; a result near 24% requires a denominator of approximately 77,000 SF, which has no support anywhere in the record. This is the clearest arithmetic failure in the Report, and it is outcome-determinative: it converts a conclusion of comfortable compliance into a **5.58 percentage-point violation** of a condition the Board must find satisfied before it can approve the use.")
label_par("Consequence.", "The warehouse/flex use cannot be approved as configured. The shortfall can be cured in one of three ways, each with different consequences: reduce the warehouse/flex floor area in Building B to 15,125 SF or less; reallocate floor area so that total GFA rises without increasing warehouse/flex area (for example by adding a permitted use elsewhere, which would also need to satisfy the FAR, coverage and parking standards); or obtain relief from the conditional use standard, which requires a variance and is in any event discretionary. Standing alone this issue would prevent a conditional use approval; combined with C-3 it means the use has no approval at all.")
label_par("Required action.", "Recompute the ratio and require the Seller to identify the basis for the 24% figure. Any cure should be modelled against the parking requirement, because reducing warehouse area changes the § 245-42(b) parking calculation.")

# ---- C-3 ----
H2("4.3  C-3 — No Planning Board conditional use approval for the warehouse/flex use")
label_par("What the Report says.", "Section V.C concludes: \"No conditional use approval from the Planning Board **appears to be required** beyond the conditions satisfied by the site as currently configured.\" The Report's Section V.B nevertheless classifies the warehouse/flex use correctly as a \"Conditional Use\" under § 245-15(c)(3).")
label_par("What the record shows.", "Section 245-15(c) provides that conditional uses are permitted \"subject to **approval by the Planning Board** upon a finding that the conditions specified herein and the general conditional use standards of § 245-22 are satisfied,\" and that \"The Planning Board may impose reasonable conditions upon any conditional use approval.\" The variance resolution addresses the point twice and without ambiguity. Paragraph 2(5) finds that the warehouse/flex use \"is classified as a conditional use ... and that the Applicant has indicated its intention to seek, or will be required to obtain, **separate conditional use approval** from the Maplewood Planning Board in connection with that use,\" and states that the variance relief \"**does not constitute, and shall not be construed as, conditional use approval**, site plan approval, or any other form of land use approval other than the specific bulk variance described herein.\" Condition 5 independently obliges the Applicant to obtain \"conditional use approval for the warehouse/flex use from the Maplewood Planning Board.\" The Report itself lists the resolution among the documents reviewed and summarises it at Section VI and Appendix B — but omits paragraph 2(5) and Condition 5 entirely.")
label_par("Analysis.", "There are only three possibilities, and the Report reconciles none of them. Either a conditional use approval exists and was not produced, or it does not exist and the use has been operating since 2014 without the approval the ordinance requires, or the Report's view that no approval is needed is correct — which would contradict both § 245-15(c) and the Board's express findings. The first is a document request; the second is the most likely and is a live zoning violation; the third is not tenable. The Report's closing sentence — that no conditional use approval \"appears to be required\" — is an assertion of legal conclusion that the Report elsewhere disclaims the competence to make (Section 2.3(2) states that the Report \"does not constitute a legal opinion\").")
label_par("Consequence.", "The warehouse/flex use is a conditional use operating without conditional use approval. It is therefore neither a permitted use nor an approved conditional use, and § 245-15(d)(7) provides that any use not expressly listed as a permitted principal use, permitted accessory use or conditional use \"shall be deemed prohibited.\" The use is exposed to enforcement under § 245-62, including per-diem penalties, and no certificate of compliance could properly have issued for Building B under § 245-60(b), which forbids issuance until \"all conditions of approval have been satisfied.\" A Planning Board application is required, and it cannot succeed as configured because of C-2 and H-2.")
label_par("Required action.", "Request from the Seller the complete conditional use file, including any Planning Board resolution and the site plan approval said to underlie the 2014 construction. Absent production, treat the use as unapproved and make conditional use approval a Closing condition.")

# ---- C-4 ----
H2("4.4  C-4 — The variance is personal to the Seller and expires on transfer")
label_par("What the Report says.", "Section VI states that \"The Board's resolution memorializes these conditions as binding obligations running with the variance approval. **The variance remains in effect and the property benefits from this approval.**\" Section I and Section IX.A each rely on the variance as the sole qualification to an otherwise unqualified finding of compliance. Appendix B summarises the resolution as granting \"a reduced east side yard setback of 18 feet\" and says nothing further. The Report nowhere mentions transferability, and it does not mention the 90-day confirmation mechanism at all.")
label_par("What the record shows.", "Section 4 of the resolution provides that the variance \"is **personal to the Applicant**, Maplewood Gateway Associates LP, and its principals,\" and that it \"shall expire automatically upon the occurrence of\" either \"(a) the approved use is discontinued for a period of twelve (12) consecutive months\" or \"(b) **the property is transferred, conveyed, assigned, or otherwise alienated** to any person or entity other than the Applicant ... **UNLESS the successor owner, transferee, or assignee files an application with this Board for confirmation of the variance within ninety (90) days of the date of transfer**.\" It continues: \"Failure to file such application within the ninety (90) day period shall result in the **automatic expiration** of this variance, and the property shall thereafter be required to comply with the full setback requirements of § 245-18.\" The Board also \"reserves the right, upon any such confirmation application, to impose additional or modified conditions.\" The Survey flags the point twice — in the surveyor's note at Section 1 and again at Section 10.1(8) — and expressly declines to opine on it.")
label_par("Analysis.", "The sale to Crescent Boulevard Holdings LLC is a transfer within limb (b). On Closing the variance expires by its own terms unless the Buyer files a confirmation application within 90 days, and even then the Board may impose additional or modified conditions. Two points follow. First, the Report's phrase \"binding obligations running with the variance approval\" glosses the distinction that matters: under § 245-58(b) the **conditions** bind successors and assigns, but under § 4 of the resolution the **variance itself** does not run with the land. Second, without the variance the east side yard setback of 19.0 ft (Survey, Section 4) stands against the enhanced 25-foot requirement of § 245-18(h)(2) — a **6.0-foot deficiency** with no relief of any kind.")
P("The practical consequence is larger than the setback itself. Without the variance, Building B becomes at best a nonconforming structure under § 245-55(d), which may be \"maintained and repaired but shall not be enlarged, extended, reconstructed, or structurally altered\" unless the work conforms to current requirements. That would sterilise the very expansion the Report promotes. Section IX.B(2) of the Report tells the Buyer that the FAR of 0.3307 against a 1.50 maximum indicates \"significant remaining development capacity\" and that \"Any future expansion or development would have considerable room within the existing FAR limitations.\" That advice is materially incomplete: the binding constraint on expansion is not FAR but the east side yard, and the relief that makes the east side yard tolerable lapses on Closing.")
label_par("Consequence.", "The property's only dimensional relief is time-limited and conditional on action by the Buyer after Closing. If the confirmation application is not filed by roughly **November 13, 2025** (90 days from an August 15, 2025 Closing), the variance expires automatically and cannot be revived by the Buyer without a fresh application. Both the east setback and Building B's development potential are at stake.")
label_par("Required action.", "Make the variance's survival a Closing condition. The Seller should either procure a fresh variance that runs with the land, or join with the Buyer in a confirmation application to the Board under § 4, with the Buyer participating so as to be heard on any additional conditions. The Buyer should also calendar the 90-day deadline on the day of Closing, and consider whether the PSA's 24-month survival period for the § 5.3 zoning representations (PSA § 5.7) is long enough to reach a lapsed variance.")

# ---- C-5 ----
H2("4.5  C-5 — The east landscape buffer fails on width and on species")
label_par("What the Report says.", "Section IV.B records \"Landscaped Buffer — East | Required per variance condition | Landscape buffer exists along the eastern boundary | **COMPLIANT**.\" Section IV.C states that \"A landscape buffer is maintained along the eastern property boundary **in accordance with this condition**.\" Section VI, addressing compliance with Condition 1, states that \"a landscape buffer is maintained along the eastern property boundary in accordance with this condition.\" Section IX.A records \"Landscape Buffer — East | COMPLIANT.\"")
label_par("What the record shows.", "Condition 1 of the resolution requires a \"**fifteen (15) foot wide evergreen landscape buffer** along the entire eastern property boundary,\" consisting of \"a minimum of one (1) evergreen tree per eight (8) linear feet of boundary, with a minimum planting height of six (6) feet at the time of installation, supplemented by evergreen shrubs planted in staggered rows to create a continuous visual screen achieving a minimum opacity of seventy-five percent (75%) within two (2) growing seasons,\" on a landscape plan prepared by a licensed landscape architect and \"submitted to the Borough Zoning Officer for review and approval prior to the issuance of a Certificate of Occupancy for Building B.\" Section 245-18(i) independently requires a 15-foot buffer planted with a mix of evergreen trees and shrubs sufficient to provide year-round screening to a minimum height of six feet within three years.")
P("The Survey, at Section 7, measured the buffer at three cross-sections: **11.8 ft** at the north end, **12.2 ft** at the midpoint and **12.0 ft** at the south end, for an **average of 12.0 ft**. It records that the plantings are \"sparse deciduous trees and shrubs, predominantly maple (__Acer__ spp.) and ornamental cherry (__Prunus__ spp.),\" that \"**No evergreen species were identified** along the buffer at the time of the field survey,\" that there was \"No continuous ground cover planting,\" and that \"No fencing was observed.\" The surveyor notes that the measured width is \"3.0 feet less than the required 15.0 feet\" and that the plantings are \"predominantly deciduous rather than evergreen.\" The ESA, at Section 4, independently recorded a buffer \"approximately 12 feet in width, consisting primarily of deciduous shrubs.\" (It did so expressly without addressing zoning compliance, as it was entitled to do.)")
label_par("Analysis.", "Three of the four elements of Condition 1 fail on the face of the field evidence: **width** (12.0 ft against 15.0 ft, a 20% shortfall sustained across all three cross-sections and not attributable to a single narrow point); **composition** (no evergreen species at all, where evergreens are the specified and only acceptable means of achieving year-round screening); and **continuous screen** (sparse plantings, no continuous ground cover, opacity untested but plainly not 75%). A fourth element — whether the licensed landscape architect's plan was approved by the Zoning Officer before the Building B certificate of occupancy issued — cannot be tested on the record before us and is carried as a document request.")
P("The Report's method is the source of the error. It did not measure the buffer; it did not commission a measurement; and it conducted no site visit (Section 2.3(5) of the Report confirms this). It asserted compliance from the existence of vegetation. The Survey, which the Report relies on for every other dimension in the document, contains the contradictory measurement in a section the Report does not cite.")
label_par("Consequence.", "This is a breach of a condition of variance approval, and § 245-62(a) provides that a violation of \"any condition of a variance approval\" is subject to the penalties established by N.J.S.A. 40:55D-18, with each day after a notice to cure constituting a separate offence. More importantly for the transaction, the buffer is the consideration on which the Board's findings rest. Finding 2 of the resolution grants relief \"provided that adequate buffering and screening is installed along the entire eastern boundary\" and finds that \"the conditions imposed herein will adequately protect\" the neighbouring residents. A deficient buffer therefore does two things at once: it is an enforceable violation, and it supplies the Board with a ready basis to impose additional or modified conditions on the § 4 confirmation application — a live risk given C-4.")
label_par("Required action.", "Either restore the buffer to Condition 1 (15.0 ft clear width, one evergreen per 8 linear feet at 6 ft minimum installation height, staggered evergreen shrubs to 75% opacity) with Zoning Officer sign-off, or obtain a modification of Condition 1 from the Board. Restoration should be costed as part of the cure package, since the eastern boundary also carries the 19-foot building setback that limits any re-grading.")

# ---- C-6 ----
H2("4.6  C-6 — Monument sign exceeds the B-3 height and area limits; the Report applied the wrong district's standards")
label_par("What the Report says.", "Section VIII.A correctly states the B-3 standard: monument signs are subject to \"maximum sign height of 6 feet above finished grade; maximum sign face area of 32 square feet.\" Section VIII.B then records the existing monument sign as \"8 ft height, 48 SF face\" and certifies it \"**COMPLIANT**.\" Section VIII.C states that \"The monument sign is consistent with the character of the B-3 district\" and that the sign \"was permitted under the building permit records reviewed.\" Section IX.A records \"Signage | COMPLIANT.\"")
label_par("What the record shows.", "Section 245-50(c)(1)(ii) limits monument sign height to \"**six (6) feet** measured from the finished grade at the base of the sign to the highest point of the sign structure,\" inclusive of \"the base and all structural and decorative elements.\" Subsection (iii) limits sign face area to \"**thirty-two (32) square feet per side**.\" The Survey, at Section 3.1, records the monument sign as having \"a measured height of 8 feet and a sign face area of approximately 48 square feet (double-faced).\"")
label_par("Analysis.", "The sign exceeds both limits: **2 feet over on height (33% over)** and **16 square feet over on area per side (50% over)**. The explanation is visible on the face of the Report. Eight feet and 48 square feet are precisely the monument sign standards for the adjoining **B-2 General Business District**, set out at § 245-50(d)(1). The Report has taken its statement of the governing standard from the B-3 subsection and its determination of compliance from the B-2 subsection, and the contradiction sits within a single two-page section. That is not a matter of interpretation; § 245-50(c) is expressly confined to the B-3 district.")
P("Nor is the sign saved by the nonconforming-sign provisions. Section 245-50(i) protects a sign \"lawfully erected prior to the adoption or amendment of this section,\" but a nonconforming sign \"may continue to be maintained but shall not be enlarged, relocated, or structurally altered,\" and must be removed if abandoned or if the associated use is discontinued for 90 days. Even on the most favourable view — that the sign was lawfully permitted in 2014 under a standard then permitting eight feet — it is a nonconforming sign, not a compliant one, and the Report's certification is wrong in either case. We flag the 2014 permit position as an open question at Section 10 (OQ-2).")
label_par("Consequence.", "The sign requires physical reduction, replacement, or a variance, and a sign permit under § 245-50 (which requires a Construction Official's sign permit for all signs not exempt under § 245-50(h) — the Report instead cites \"building permit records,\" which is a different instrument). The exposure is modest in cost but the issue matters because it is one of three items the Report certifies as compliant on the basis on an incorrect statement of the governing standard, which goes to the weight of the Report as a whole.")
label_par("Required action.", "Require the Seller to produce the sign permit history and either reduce the sign to 6 ft and 32 SF per side or obtain a variance; and require a corrected sign compliance statement covering the additional matters at M-5.")
PYEOF

tool_calls.name: bash
tool_calls.arguments:
{"command": "cd "$WORKSPACE_DIR"; cat > build/p6_high.py <<'PYEOF'
# ================= 5. HIGH ISSUES =================
doc.add_page_break()
H1("High-Severity Issues", "5")
P("The issues below are material departures from a regulated standard, or material gaps in the analysis, that are capable of cure by an administrative step, a targeted variance, or a physical correction. Each feeds into the § 10.3(g) closing deliverable, because each bears on whether conditions of approval have been satisfied and whether approvals remain in full force.")

H2("5.1  H-1 — There is no landscape buffer at all along the north boundary")
label_par("What the Report says.", "Section IV.A correctly states the rule: \"The 15-foot landscape buffer requirement applies along **any property boundary that abuts a residential zone**, independent of the setback standards.\" Having stated it correctly, the Report applies it to the east boundary only. Section IV.B contains a single buffer row (\"Landscaped Buffer — East\"); Section IV.C discusses the east buffer alone; Section VI addresses Condition 1 of the variance, which is also east-only.")
label_par("What the record shows.", "Section 245-18(i) requires that where a lot in the B-3 district abuts a residential zone, \"a landscaped buffer strip not less than fifteen (15) feet in width shall be provided along **the entire length of the property line abutting the residential zone**,\" and that \"The buffer area shall not contain any structures, parking spaces, driveways, loading areas, or stormwater management facilities.\" The Survey, at Section 2, states that the property is bounded \"on the north by Lots 5 and 6, Block 413 (R-4 Residential zone)\" and at Note 2 confirms those lots are \"classified R-4 Residential.\" The north boundary therefore abuts R-4 and attracts its own 15-foot buffer — a requirement that exists independently of the 2013 variance, which was directed only at the eastern boundary.")
P("What occupies the north boundary instead, according to the Survey, is a 40 × 25 ft loading dock apron \"facing the rear (north) property boundary and the R-4 Residential zone,\" a 20-foot-wide driveway at the northwest corner serving Curb Cut No. 3 from Elm Terrace, and — on the ESA's observation — \"a portion of the rear parking area\" extending into the northeast corner.")
label_par("Analysis.", "The Report articulates the correct rule and then applies it to one of two boundaries that engage it. The omission is not formal: the north buffer zone is occupied by the three uses § 245-18(i) expressly excludes from a buffer — a loading area, a driveway and parking — so the requirement is not merely unfulfilled but affirmatively defeated.")
label_par("Consequence.", "A distinct violation of § 245-18(i) on the north boundary, additional to the east-buffer violation at C-5 and the rear setback violation at C-1. The three issues share a physical solution on the north boundary and should be designed and costed together.")
label_par("Required action.", "Require a site plan overlay of the 15-foot buffer on all boundaries abutting R-4, and a landscape plan that reconciles the buffer with the loading, driveway and parking areas now occupying it.")

H2("5.2  H-2 — The loading dock and apron are wholly unscreened and sit in a yard where loading is prohibited")
label_par("What the Report says.", "Section V.C(b), addressing conditional use condition (b) on screening, contains no analysis of screening at all. It states only that \"The site layout provides for loading activity associated with the warehouse/flex use in Building B. Loading access is facilitated by the existing curb cuts and internal circulation drives. The site plan accommodates the operational needs of the warehouse/flex use within the overall site design.\" The Report then certifies condition (b) satisfied as part of its blanket conclusion that the use complies with \"all applicable conditions of § 245-15(c)(3).\"")
label_par("What the record shows.", "Section 245-15(c)(3)(b) requires that \"All truck loading areas, loading docks, and service areas shall be screened from adjacent residential zones by a **solid fence or wall not less than six (6) feet in height supplemented by evergreen plantings**, such that the loading operations are not visible from any residential property or residential zone boundary,\" and that the screening \"shall be installed **prior to the commencement** of the warehouse, distribution, or flex space use and shall be perpetually maintained.\" Section 245-42(g)(5) imposes a parallel requirement, and adds that \"Where a loading area is located within one hundred (100) feet of a residential zone boundary, the screening requirement shall apply **regardless of intervening topography, structures, or vegetation**.\" Section 245-18(h)(3) prohibits loading areas within the enhanced rear yard altogether.")
P("The Survey records, at Sections 3.2 and 6, \"One at-grade loading dock and apron area ... on the north side of Building B, facing the rear (north) property boundary and the R-4 Residential zone. The loading dock apron area measures approximately 40 feet by 25 feet. **No screening wall, fence, or landscape screening structures were observed** surrounding or adjacent to the loading dock area at the time of the field survey.\" The conditional use was commenced in 2014; the screening, if it ever existed, was required to be installed before commencement.")
label_par("Analysis.", "This is a failure to analyse a mandatory condition, presented as a finding that the condition is satisfied. Four separate requirements fail on the field evidence: the 6-foot solid fence or wall (absent); the evergreen supplement (absent); the pre-commencement installation (cannot have occurred, since nothing is there); and the perpetual maintenance obligation. Separately, the apron is 25 feet deep and abuts the residential boundary directly, so it is unquestionably within 100 feet of the R-4 zone and within the enhanced rear yard. Because condition (b) is a condition that the Planning Board must find satisfied before approving the conditional use, this issue independently defeats the conditional use in its present configuration and compounds C-3.")
P("We note a conflict in the record on orientation that should be resolved before any application is prepared: the Survey places the dock on the **north** side of Building B, while the ESA, at Section 4, records \"A loading dock was observed on the **west** side of Building B.\" The distinction is not academic — it determines which yard and which enhanced standard apply, and whether the loading area is prohibited outright under § 245-18(h)(3). This is carried as open question OQ-3.")
label_par("Consequence.", "Breach of § 245-15(c)(3)(b), § 245-42(g)(5) and § 245-18(h)(3). Cure requires either a 6-foot masonry wall or solid fence supplemented with evergreens, or relocation of the loading function — the latter being constrained by the rear and east setbacks.")
label_par("Required action.", "Include in the cure package: a screening design meeting § 245-15(c)(3)(b) and § 245-42(g)(5), a verification of the dock's true orientation, and a variance addressing any loading area that remains within the enhanced rear yard.")

H2("5.3  H-3 — Off-street loading was never analysed; the site provides one space against five required")
label_par("What the Report says.", "Nothing. Section VII is titled \"Off-Street Parking Compliance\" and addresses parking ratios only. Section 245-42 is titled \"Off-Street Parking **and Loading** Requirements,\" and the Report cites it as the governing provision without addressing its loading subsections. Loading appears in the Report only as a descriptive phrase in Section V.C(b) (\"Loading access is facilitated by the existing curb cuts\").")

label_par("Analysis.", "On the Report's own floor areas the site is short by four loading spaces. Two caveats should be stated rather than assumed. label_par("What the Report says.", "Section VIII.A states the standard correctly: \"A maximum of 2 wall signs per building is permitted.\" Section VIII.B then lists three separate Building A wall signs — Sign 1, Sign 2 and Sign 3, each approximately 20 SF — each marked \"COMPLIANT (area).\" Section VIII.C concludes that \"Wall signage for Building A is within the maximum allowable area per § 245-50.\"")
label_par("What the record shows.", "Section 245-50(c)(2)(i): \"Each building shall be permitted a maximum of **two (2) wall signs**. label_par("What the record shows.", "The ESA, at Section 4, records that \"Retail tenants occupying ground-floor spaces at the time of the reconnaissance included a **fitness studio**, a coffee shop, and an insurance office.\" Section 245-15(a) enumerates the permitted principal uses in B-3: retail sales establishments; professional and business offices; personal service establishments (\"barber shops, hair salons, beauty parlors, dry cleaning and laundry pick-up establishments ..., tailors, and shoe repair shops\"); banks and financial institutions; restaurants, \"subject to site plan approval by the Planning Board pursuant to § 245-30\"; mixed-use structures; public and quasi-public uses; and parking structures. H2("5.6  H-6 — The Buyer has no right to rely on the Report, and the Report ignores the ESA's recognised environmental condition")
P("This issue has three limbs, and they point in the same direction: the Buyer's real protection must come from the Seller's contractual representations and from a Buyer-commissioned review, not from the Report.")

H2("5.7  H-7 — The PSA zoning representations and the closing deliverable cannot be reconciled with the record")

mktable(
    ["PSA provision", "Representation (abridged)", "Conflict with the record", "See"],

         "Warehouse/flex is a **conditional** use and no conditional use approval exists (or has been produced).", "C-3"],
        ["§ 5.3(c)", "\"All necessary zoning approvals, variances, and permits ... are in full force and effect and are **transferable to Buyer**.\"",
         "The variance is personal to the Seller and expires automatically on transfer unless a confirmation application is filed within 90 days.", "C-4"],
        ["§ 5.3(d)", "\"To Seller's actual knowledge, there are no conditions of any zoning approval or variance ... that are in default or that have not been satisfied.\"",
         "Condition 1 (15 ft evergreen buffer) is not satisfied: the buffer is 12.0 ft and deciduous. Conditions 2 and 3 are unverified.", "C-5"],
        ["§ 5.3(f)", "The variance authorising a reduced east side yard setback of \"**twelve feet (12')**\" \"is valid and in full force and effect\" and has not been modified or revoked.",
         "The resolution grants **eighteen (18) feet**, not twelve; and validity is subject to the transfer expiry in § 4 of the resolution.", "C-4, L-3"],
        ["§ 5.5", "To Seller's actual knowledge the property and its use \"comply in all material respects\" with all laws including the Zoning Ordinance.",
         "Substantial non-compliance is documented at C-1, C-2, C-6, H-1, H-2, H-3 and H-4.", "Multiple"],
        ["§ 10.3(g)", "At Closing the Seller must deliver \"evidence satisfactory to Buyer and Buyer's counsel that **all conditions of such approvals have been satisfied** and that such approvals remain in full force and effect.\"",
         "Cannot be delivered while the buffer condition is breached and no conditional use approval exists.", "C-3, C-4, C-5"],
        ["§ 5.4(b)", "The Phase I ESA was \"prepared for Seller\" and bears Project No. \"GE-2025-0441.\"",
         "The ESA is addressed to the **Buyer** and bears Project No. **GEC-2025-0147**.", "L-1"],
    ],
    [Inches(0.72), Inches(2.20), Inches(2.80), Inches(0.78)],
    align=["c", "l", "l", "c"], font=7.8, hdr_font=8.0)

spacer(3)
label_par("Analysis.", "Two features of Article V limit the value of these representations to the Buyer. First, the knowledge qualifier is deliberately narrow: \"to Seller's actual knowledge\" is defined in Article V as \"the current, conscious awareness of Lorraine DiMartino ... **without any duty of inquiry**, investigation, or review of files or records.\" A qualification of that kind gives little protection where the Seller has chosen not to inquire. Second, § 5.3(e) distances the Seller from the very document that is supposed to carry the analysis. The combination means the Buyer's practical protection lies in the objective representations — § 5.3(b), (c) and (f) are not knowledge-qualified — and in the remedies under Article VIII.")
P("There is also a procedural point that should not be missed. Under § 8.3(d)(ii) the zoning ordinances of the Borough are a Permitted Exception only \"**provided that the Property is in compliance therewith**, subject to Seller's representations.\" Where the property is not in compliance, the zoning ordinance does not qualify as a Permitted Exception, and the § 8.4 covenant to convey free and clear of all encumbrances and defects except the Permitted Exceptions is engaged. That gives the Buyer a route to treat zoning non-compliance as a Title/Survey Objection under § 8.3(a) — which must be delivered by the earlier of 30 days after receipt of the Title Commitment and Survey or **July 18, 2025** — and so to preserve the termination and deposit-return remedy in § 8.3(c).")
label_par("Consequence.", "As matters stand the Seller cannot satisfy § 10.3(g), and the § 5.3 representations are, on the record, inaccurate. label_par("Required action.", "Deliver a specific written objection under § 8.3(a) before July 18, 2025 identifying each item in the table above; require cure as a condition precedent to Closing; and negotiate a special indemnity outside the § 5.7 cap together with a Closing holdback sized to the cure cost.")
PYEOF
python3 -c "print('p6 ok')""}

But the Survey is certified to Crescent Boulevard Holdings LLC, Ridgeline Title & Escrow, Briarcliff National Bank and Holloway Stern LLP, and states that it \"may not be relied upon by any other party without the prior written consent of Cartwright Surveying Associates.\" The Seller's consultant has therefore relied on an instrument it is not on its face entitled to rely upon, while producing a report the Buyer is not entitled to rely upon. Neither document is presently usable by both parties.")
label_par("(c) The environmental condition.", "Section V.C(c) of the Report states that \"we are not aware of any hazardous materials being stored on the property in connection with the warehouse/flex use\" and that \"this condition is considered satisfied based on available records.\" The ESA identifies **REC-1**: tetrachloroethylene from the former dry cleaning operation at 1881 Crescent Boulevard (approximately 1978–2009), listed on the NJDEP Known Contaminated Sites list under Program Interest No. 007624 with a status of \"Pending\"; documented groundwater flow \"generally east-northeast — that is, from the contamination source toward the subject property\"; monitoring wells observed within 15 to 20 feet of the shared boundary; and a recommendation for a Phase II including sub-slab soil vapour sampling beneath both buildings. The Report does not list the ESA among the documents it reviewed (Section II.2.2).")
P("We should be precise about what this does and does not establish. Section 245-15(c)(3)(c) prohibits the **storage** of hazardous materials on the premises; contamination migrating from an adjoining property is not \"storage,\" so the conditional use condition is not necessarily breached. The defect in the Report is different and still material: it pronounced the condition satisfied \"based on available records\" without having the one record that bears on it, and without acknowledging that the property may be affected by a contaminant plume migrating toward it. A conclusion of compliance that is reached without the governing environmental report is not a conclusion the Buyer should accept, particularly where the same consultant's report is the Buyer's only zoning diligence. The separate and distinct failure to address the annual certification required by the same subsection is at M-10.")
label_par("Consequence.", "The Report cannot be the basis of the Buyer's decision. Either the reliance defects are cured, or the Buyer must commission its own zoning review and rest on the PSA representations.")
label_par("Required action.", "Obtain (i) a reliance letter from Pinnacle Land Advisors Inc. running to the Buyer, its counsel and its lender; (ii) a recertification of the Survey, or the surveyor's written consent to reliance by the Seller and Pinnacle; and (iii) a Buyer-commissioned zoning and land use review that integrates the ESA findings. Do not treat the Report as a Seller representation.")

H2("5.7  H-7 — The PSA zoning representations and the closing deliverable cannot be reconciled with the record")
P("The Report's errors would matter less if the Seller's own representations were sound. They are not. The table below sets each relevant representation against the record. Each of these representations survives Closing for **24 months** (PSA § 5.7), subject to an aggregate cap of 10% of the Purchase Price, or **$1,850,000**.")
mktable(
    ["PSA provision", "Representation (abridged)", "Conflict with the record", "See"],
    [
        ["§ 5.3(b)", "Current \"retail, office, and warehouse/flex uses\" are permitted uses in B-3 \"or have been duly approved by the appropriate municipal boards.\"",
         "Warehouse/flex is a **conditional** use and no conditional use approval exists (or has been produced).", "C-3"],
        ["§ 5.3(c)", "\"All necessary zoning approvals, variances, and permits ... are in full force and effect and are **transferable to Buyer**.\"",
         "The variance is personal to the Seller and expires automatically on transfer unless a confirmation application is filed within 90 days.", "C-4"],
        ["§ 5.3(d)", "\"To Seller's actual knowledge, there are no conditions of any zoning approval or variance ... that are in default or that have not been satisfied.\"",
         "Condition 1 (15 ft evergreen buffer) is not satisfied: the buffer is 12.0 ft and deciduous. Conditions 2 and 3 are unverified.", "C-5"],
        ["§ 5.3(f)", "The variance authorising a reduced east side yard setback of \"**twelve feet (12')**\" \"is valid and in full force and effect\" and has not been modified or revoked.",
         "The resolution grants **eighteen (18) feet**, not twelve; and validity is subject to the transfer expiry in § 4 of the resolution.", "C-4, L-3"],
        ["§ 5.5", "To Seller's actual knowledge the property and its use \"comply in all material respects\" with all laws including the Zoning Ordinance.",
         "Substantial non-compliance is documented at C-1, C-2, C-6, H-1, H-2, H-3 and H-4.", "Multiple"],
        ["§ 10.3(g)", "At Closing the Seller must deliver \"evidence satisfactory to Buyer and Buyer's counsel that **all conditions of such approvals have been satisfied** and that such approvals remain in full force and effect.\"",
         "Cannot be delivered while the buffer condition is breached and no conditional use approval exists.", "C-3, C-4, C-5"],
        ["§ 5.4(b)", "The Phase I ESA was \"prepared for Seller\" and bears Project No. \"GE-2025-0441.\"",
         "The ESA is addressed to the **Buyer** and bears Project No. **GEC-2025-0147**.", "L-1"],
    ],
    [Inches(0.72), Inches(2.20), Inches(2.80), Inches(0.78)],
    align=["c", "l", "l", "c"], font=7.8, hdr_font=8.0)

spacer(3)
label_par("Analysis.", "Two features of Article V limit the value of these representations to the Buyer. First, the knowledge qualifier is deliberately narrow: \"to Seller's actual knowledge\" is defined in Article V as \"the current, conscious awareness of Lorraine DiMartino ... **without any duty of inquiry**, investigation, or review of files or records.\" A qualification of that kind gives little protection where the Seller has chosen not to inquire. Second, § 5.3(e) distances the Seller from the very document that is supposed to carry the analysis. The combination means the Buyer's practical protection lies in the objective representations — § 5.3(b), (c) and (f) are not knowledge-qualified — and in the remedies under Article VIII.")
P("There is also a procedural point that should not be missed. Under § 8.3(d)(ii) the zoning ordinances of the Borough are a Permitted Exception only \"**provided that the Property is in compliance therewith**, subject to Seller's representations.\" Where the property is not in compliance, the zoning ordinance does not qualify as a Permitted Exception, and the § 8.4 covenant to convey free and clear of all encumbrances and defects except the Permitted Exceptions is engaged. That gives the Buyer a route to treat zoning non-compliance as a Title/Survey Objection under § 8.3(a) — which must be delivered by the earlier of 30 days after receipt of the Title Commitment and Survey or **July 18, 2025** — and so to preserve the termination and deposit-return remedy in § 8.3(c).")
label_par("Consequence.", "As matters stand the Seller cannot satisfy § 10.3(g), and the § 5.3 representations are, on the record, inaccurate. The Buyer's remedies are otherwise confined to a post-closing damages claim inside a $1,850,000 cap, on a 24-month survival period, subject to the narrow knowledge qualifier.")
label_par("Required action.", "Deliver a specific written objection under § 8.3(a) before July 18, 2025 identifying each item in the table above; require cure as a condition precedent to Closing; and negotiate a special indemnity outside the § 5.7 cap together with a Closing holdback sized to the cure cost.")
