states that the sign "was permitted under the building permit records reviewed"; §
245-50 requires a sign permit from the Construction Official for all signs not exempt
under § 245-50(h), which is a different instrument from a building permit.
Action. Test each requirement and obtain the sign permit file. The result may add to
the cure cost or may supply a basis to contest the C-6 deficiency.

6.6 M-6 — Building B's wall-sign frontage basis is unsupported and the
facade is misdescribed
Finding. The Report measures Building B's wall-sign allowance against "a primary
frontage facing the internal parking lot of approximately 100 linear feet" (100 × 1.5
= 150 SF). No such dimension appears in the Survey or anywhere else in the record,
and the Survey records the sign on the "south-facing (parking lot side) facade"
whereas the Report places it on the "west façade." More fundamentally, § 245-50(a)
defines "building frontage" as "the linear measurement of the building wall facing a
public street" and, for buildings not facing a public street, as "the linear
measurement of the building wall containing the primary entrance." Building B
does not face a public street on the side in question, so the parking-lot wall is the
wrong measure.
The 32 SF sign will very likely comply on any plausible frontage — a frontage as short
as 25 feet would still permit 37.5 SF — so we do not rank this as a violation. It is
ranked as Moderate because the Report has arrived at a compliance conclusion
through an invented dimension and a misidentified facade, which is the same pattern
of reasoning that produced C-6 and materially affects the weight the Buyer can place
on the signage section.
Action. Measure Building B's frontage to the wall containing its primary entrance and
restate the allowance.

headroom is one foot
Finding. Section 245-18(d) limits height to 45 feet or 3 stories, whichever is less, and
permits rooftop mechanical equipment, penthouses and stairway bulkheads to exceed
the limit by not more than 10 feet, provided they are set back from the building
perimeter by at least their own height above the roofline and occupy not more than
20% of the total roof area. The Survey measures Building A at "44 feet, measured
from average finished grade at the building perimeter to the highest point of the roof
structure (parapet cap)," and records that "rooftop mechanical equipment [was]
observed behind the parapet." The measurement therefore excludes the equipment.
With only one foot of headroom to the 45-foot limit, any unit projecting more than a
foot above the parapet engages the appurtenance allowance, whose two conditions
have not been tested.

Action. Obtain elevations or an as-built survey showing the height of the rooftop
equipment above the parapet, its setback from the perimeter, and the roof area it
occupies. Although the building satisfies the 3-story limb, the footage limit applies
independently.

6.8 M-8 — Floodplain, drainage easement and stormwater facilities in the
rear yard
Finding. The Survey records that approximately 0.3 acres (13,068 SF) of the
northeast corner lies within FEMA Flood Zone AE with a base flood elevation of 42.0
feet NAVD88, extending about 75 feet along the north boundary and 175 feet along the
east boundary, and that the area is "covered by turf grass and a portion of the rear
parking area." It records a 15-foot drainage easement in the same northeast corner
in favour of the Essex County Flood Control and Drainage Authority, overlapping the
flood zone. The ESA confirms the area is at lower grade with hydric soil indicators and
sediment deposits on pavement near the Elm Terrace curb cut.
Section 245-18(h)(3) permits only landscaping and stormwater management
facilities expressly approved by the Planning Board within the enhanced rear
yard, and § 245-18(i) prohibits stormwater facilities within the landscaped buffer — a
tension that must be resolved by design rather than assumed. The Report disclaims
flood matters (Section 2.3(3) and Section X), which is defensible as a matter of scope,
but its Recommendation 2 on "significant remaining development capacity" does not
account for the fact that roughly 13,068 SF is both floodplain and easement-burdened,
or that rear parking appears to sit within the prohibited rear-yard zone.
Action. Obtain the site plan and any stormwater approval; confirm whether any
stormwater facility lies within the enhanced rear yard or the buffer, and whether it was
expressly approved by the Planning Board. Have a design professional confirm the
floodplain and flood-hazard status against the current effective FIRM panel (see L-2).

6.9 M-9 — No certificate of compliance or zoning permit is established
Finding. Section 245-60(a) prohibits construction or a change of use without a zoning
permit, and § 245-60(b) prohibits occupancy until the Zoning Officer issues a
certificate of compliance confirming conformity with Chapter 245 "including all
conditions of any variance approval, conditional use approval, or site plan
approval," and provides that the Zoning Officer "shall not issue a certificate of
compliance until all conditions of approval have been satisfied." The Report relies
throughout on "Certificate of Occupancy records" — a different instrument, which is
not evidence of zoning compliance — and does not identify any record by date or
number. If the buffer condition, the loading screening condition and the conditions of a
conditional use were unsatisfied, no valid certificate of compliance ought to have
issued for Building B.
Action. Obtain the complete zoning permit and certificate of compliance file for both
buildings under § 245-60(c). This is the single most probative document request in the
matter.

6.10 M-10 — The annual hazardous-materials certification has never been
evidenced
Finding. Section 245-15(c)(3)(c) does not merely prohibit the storage of hazardous
materials; it requires that "The applicant shall provide a certification to the
Planning Board, at the time of application and annually thereafter, that no
hazardous materials are stored on-site." Because no conditional use application was
ever made (C-3), no baseline certification exists, and no annual certification has been
filed. The Report does not mention the obligation. The Report's observation that the
consultant is "not aware" of any storage is not a certification and does not discharge it.

9.3 The three courses open to the Buyer
Course A — cure before Closing (preferred). Deliver the objections by July 18, and
make Closing conditional on the Seller having obtained the discretionary approvals
and completed the physical works, or on a holdback sufficient to fund them. This is the

the Purchase Price sized to the estimated cost of the discretionary applications and

{"file_path": "response.md", "content": "# Zoning Issues Memorandum — Summary

**Deliverable:** `zoning-issues-memorandum.docx` (38 pages, 11 sections + 2 appendices)

A source-grounded review of the seller's Zoning Compliance Report (Pinnacle Land Advisors, PLA-2025-0087, 22 Apr 2025) tested against the Chapter 245 excerpts, the ALTA/NSPS survey, Resolution ZB-2013-22, the Phase I ESA summary and the PSA excerpts.

## Method
Every source was read in full (including recitals, conditions of approval and surveyor's notes); all 33 property-level data points were tabulated against the ordinance; and **every figure in the Report was independently recomputed** — the worksheet is Appendix B, and the source-to-deliverable trace is Appendix A.

## Headline finding
The Report's conclusion of full compliance "subject to the 2013 variance" does not survive the record. **28 issues** are identified: **6 Critical, 7 High, 10 Moderate, 5 Low.**

Six critical issues:

| ID | Issue | Report said | Record shows |
|---|---|---|---|
| C-1 | Rear yard | 28 ft "COMPLIANT" vs 25 ft | § 245-18(h)(3) requires **35 ft** abutting residential — **7 ft deficient**, no variance |
| C-2 | Warehouse/flex share of GFA | "approximately 24%" | **30.58%** vs the 25% cap — 3,375 SF excess |
| C-3 | Conditional use approval | "not required" | Planning Board approval required; the resolution says so twice |
| C-4 | Variance transferability | "remains in effect" | Personal to Seller; **expires on transfer** absent a 90-day confirmation application |
| C-5 | East buffer | "COMPLIANT" | **12.0 ft, deciduous** vs 15 ft evergreen required |
| C-6 | Monument sign | 8 ft / 48 SF "COMPLIANT" | B-3 limits are **6 ft / 32 SF** (8/48 are the B-2 standards) |

## Analytical approach
- **Root cause, not just errors.** Eight misstatements and five omissions trace to one pattern: the Report transcribes base standards, or the adjoining district's standards, while omitting the enhanced "abutting residential" qualification — then states limits correctly and does not apply them. That is why the Report is not correctable by annotation.
- **Legal characterisation separated from fact.** Nonconforming-structure status under § 245-55, the conditions-vs-variance distinction under § 245-58(b), and the § 8.3(d)(ii) Permitted Exception route are flagged as legal analysis.
- **Deliberate restraint where warranted.** The PCE plume is *not* "storage" under § 245-15(c)(3)(c), so a breach is not asserted — the criticism is the Report's unqualified conclusion without the ESA. The Building B sign is treated as unsupported in basis, not noncompliant.
- **Geometry check.** The 28 ft rear-yard figure attributed to Building A is arithmetically impossible on the survey's own dimensions (~448 ft, not 28 ft), most likely a Building B measurement — carried as an open question rather than asserted.

## Transaction work product
Sections 9–11 convert findings into action: a date-critical timeline (Inspection Period closes **18 July 2025**, 73 days from the memo; Closing 15 Aug 2025; variance confirmation deadline **13 Nov 2025**), a four-track cure table, three courses open to the Buyer, 13 ranked recommendations, 10 open questions and 8 stated assumptions.

Validation: `validate.py` exit 0 (ECMA-376 schema, ZIP integrity, content types, relationships).
"}
